content.text:
Fair — I buried it. Here it is plainly.

**The decision: does SFCC-91's colour swatch go through the shared `swatch-group` component, or through a slot on `product-view`?**

That's it. Everything else follows from it.

**If shared (`swatch-group`):** you change four surfaces at once — PDP colour, PDP size, PLP tiles, recommendation carousels — because they all render through that one component. Needs Tier 2 + Squad B sign-off. And you'd be branding the size selector on the way past, which already has its own separate Figma design waiting to replace it.

**If slotted (`product-view`):** you change one surface. No Tier 2 component, no cross-squad gate, size untouched. The cost is that `product-view` gets a second additive prop, and nobody has explicitly agreed that file is allowed to become a slot host — `renderHeader` was argued for once, on its own merits.

My read: for *this story*, shared is the wrong trade. You'd pay four surfaces and two approvals to deliver one, and half of what you'd style is scheduled to be replaced.

So the only genuinely open question is the one I flagged at the end — whether you're comfortable sanctioning the second slot yourself, or want that to be a team call first.

Produce an executable build plan for SFCC-91 in the Zimmermann PWA Kit repo at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa.

All evidence below is already gathered and verified — do NOT re-gather it. Read files only to confirm specifics you need for concrete pass criteria (e.g. the exact shape of the renderHeader slot, the zimmProductStyleCode four-file pattern, the recipe guards).

Write nothing to the repo. Return the plan as your final message.

## Story
SFCC-91 — "PDP UI — Colour Swatches & Variation Selection". Story, High. Labels: Custom, DesignDependent, PRD-002, PRD-004, Squad-A.

## Acceptance criteria (from Jira, authoritative)
Swatch availability:
1. Given a product has only one colour, when the PDP loads, then the colour is displayed as a text label (e.g. "Colour: Bay Blue") and no swatches are rendered.
2. Given a product has multiple colour variations, when the PDP loads, then the index image for each colour variation is displayed as a swatch.
3. Given multiple colour swatches are displayed, when the PDP loads, then the currently viewed colour variation's swatch is visually indicated as selected.
Swatch selection:
4. Given a shopper clicks a colour swatch, when the selection is registered, then the URL updates to reflect the selected colour variation WITHOUT full page reload.
Index image not populated:
5. Given a colour variation exists but has not been enabled, when the PDP loads, then that colour variation's swatch is not rendered and the variation is not surfaced to the shopper.

## Architecture — DECIDED by Marcel, do not revisit
Per-attribute render slot on the existing product-view override. NOT a swatch-group override.

Rationale (already settled): overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:785 loops over ALL variationAttributes — colour AND size both render through base SwatchGroup/Swatch, shape chosen at line 820 by `variant={id === 'color' ? 'circle' : 'square'}`. Overriding swatch-group would therefore change PDP colour, PDP size, PLP product tiles and every recommendations carousel (base product-tile/index.jsx:29-30 imports it, and product-tile is consumed by pages/product-list and product-scroller). The size selector additionally has its own separate Figma design (pdp/size-selector, with default/filled/active/error states, and pdp/size-selector/item with in-stock/low-stock/out-of-stock/recommended/notify-me) so it will move off swatch-group anyway.

The slot must be PER-ATTRIBUTE, not per-block — a whole-block slot would put the out-of-scope size selector into this story. Signature shape:
  renderVariationAttribute?: (attr: SfccVariationAttribute) => React.ReactNode
called once inside the existing loop, defaulting to the current inline markup so behaviour is unchanged when omitted. The PDP passes an implementation that handles `id === 'color'` and returns undefined/falls through for everything else, so size renders exactly as it does today.

Precedent to mirror exactly: commit 227171e added `renderHeader?: (props: ProductViewHeaderProps) => React.ReactNode` to this same file — type on ProductViewProps (line ~178), default at the destructure (line ~283), call sites at ~692 and ~746. Read that commit and the current file before specifying this step.

## File manifest (from a completed scope-check; verdict was RISKY, rewritten prompt closed it)
CREATE (all new):
  overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx,index.test.tsx,zimmColourSwatch.css.ts}
  overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx,index.test.tsx,zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts}
MODIFY (exactly three, minimal edits):
  overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts — two imports + two keys, nothing else. TIER 2 (protectedFiles.md "Theme Component Styles", CODEOWNERS:117 → tier-2 + tier-1 approvers). Must be called out in the commit body.
  overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx — ONE new optional prop only. This is a 1069-line faithful copy-first port: no formatting, comment, type-tightening or unrelated changes.
  overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx — pass the slot only. CODEOWNERS:162 → pwa-squad-b (note: squadA.md:4,34 and squadB.md:41 both claim it for Squad A; CODEOWNERS is what actually requests review).
Expect .claude/registry/*.md to be rewritten by the PostToolUse hook on any overrides/app/ edit — that is not our write, but it will appear in git status.

## Hard exclusions
- Do NOT create or modify overrides/app/components/swatch-group/ (Tier 2, Squad B, four-surface blast radius).
- Do NOT touch overrides/app/components/image-gallery/ (Tier 2; PRD-062 gallery-updates-on-swatch-select is a separate story).
- Do NOT edit translations/*.json or overrides/app/static/translations/ (Tier 2, Integration/SI). Define i18n messages inline with intl.formatMessage, as zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx does.
- Do NOT add or change anything in overrides/app/theme/foundation/ (TIER 1, absolute per AGENTS.md Hard Rule 3). If the design needs a token that does not exist, the step must STOP and ask.
- Do NOT override, wrap or modify any hook (use-derived-product, use-variation-attributes, use-variation-params). AGENTS.md Hard Rule 5. They resolve through the hooks/index.js barrel, which does not resolve in Storybook or Vitest anyway.
- Do NOT rename the SFCC attribute id "color" to Australian spelling. Australian spelling applies to Zimmermann-authored identifiers only.

## Design (Figma: Zimmermann_Design_System_2026, fileKey wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm)
- pdp/product-colour-picker (40000307:13823) — 6 symbols: two sizes × three states.
  Large/Rectangle 48x72: State=Unselected (40000307:13826), State=Selected (40000307:13831), State=Focus (40002689:3839)
  Small/Rounded 20x24: State=Selected (40001990:51571), State=Focus (40003447:60876), State=Unselected (40001990:51851)
- Colour Options container (40001992:51881) — Type=Large (Squared) 192x104, Type=Small (Rounded) 137x56. This node is also the ">4 colours" design.
- Placement (40000307:14062, Size=Desktop Type=Default State=Default): "Colour Options" instance sits inside "Content Card and Colour Swatch" at y=126, 218x104 — between the product description and the size selector.
- NO hover state and NO disabled state exist in the design, and both absences are correct: .docs/prd/pdp.md:17 records hover-to-preview as "a custom build, not OOTB, and not scoped for go-live", and AC 5 handles unpopulated variations by not rendering them at all.
- Base square/circle variants do NOT match: a 48x72 portrait rectangle is not a square, a 20x24 rounded rect is not a circle. The recipe needs its own variant vocabulary.

## Conventions — all mechanically enforced by `npm run test`
- Recipe keys MUST be ZimmColourSwatch / ZimmColourSwatchGroup. A key named SwatchGroup would deep-merge the base SFCC recipe and fail recipeGuards.test.ts:351 (INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button','Header','ListMenu'] only).
- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts:101 — the recipe's declared `parts` must cover every part index.tsx reads off `styles.*`.
- recipeGuards.test.ts also enforces: no bare Chakra token key on a registered scale. Use var(--zimm-*) in the .css.ts recipe.
- var(--zimm-*) belongs in the recipe, NOT in JSX. Verified: 17 recipe files use it; exactly one component .tsx does (footer/footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44,62) and only inside a __css={{...styles.part, ...conditional}} spread the recipe cannot express.
- Apply styling via <chakra.x __css={styles.part}> — never sx or style props. textStyle set in the recipe, and it stays a bare key (no var() substitute for the composite expansion).
- Hooks above any early return (react-hooks/rules-of-hooks). Use `const intl = useIntl()`, never destructured (@typescript-eslint/unbound-method).
- Four-file pattern per component, mirroring overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductStyleCode/. Story title Commerce/Zimm<Name>. Vitest test scoped to the component's own contract.
- Known Vitest gap: ZimmIcon throws under Vitest (base icons barrel side effect). Mock it at the smallest surface if any component renders an icon.
- TypeScript only under overrides/. Run npx tsc --noEmit.

## Two behaviours the plan must handle explicitly
1. AC 5 ("index image not populated") is NOT the same condition as the base's `disabled={!orderable}` at line 817 — that is stock availability, this is content population. New logic either way.
2. Line 797 does `backgroundColor={name.toLowerCase()}` — using the colour's display name as a raw CSS colour keyword behind the image. "Ivory" resolves to a real CSS colour; "Bay Blue" resolves to nothing. Inherited base behaviour, marked audit-allow as verbatim. The plan must make a deliberate decision about it rather than copying it silently.

## What to return
- Goal statement.
- Scale call: multi-commit or multi-branch, with reasoning.
- File manifest with tier and owner per file.
- Ordered steps. The copy-first rule does NOT apply here (no new base-file override is being created — product-view and product-detail are already overridden), so do not invent a copy-first pause; but DO sequence so the theme registration and recipe land before the component that reads them.
- CONCRETE, checkable pass criteria per step — a command to run or an observable assertion, not "looks right".
- Per-step loop configuration for the zm-implementer/zm-tester/zm-scorer loop.
- Open questions, explicitly separated from assumptions.
- Commit breakdown, conventional-commit style. No Claude or CodeRabbit attribution anywhere in commit messages.</prompt>
</invoke>

---

## 2. Scale call

**One branch, four commits. `feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches`.**

(Deliberately *not* the other developer's branch name — this is a fresh build.)

**Why one branch, not several.** The three modified files cannot be usefully separated:

- `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` is Tier 2, but the edit is two imports + two keys. Split onto its own branch it either registers recipes that do not exist (build breaks) or creates a hard merge-order dependency between two PRs for a 4-line change. That is worse governance, not better.
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` routes to `@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b` (CODEOWNERS:162) while the theme index routes to tier-2 + tier-1 approvers. Two code-owner teams on one PR is normal and is exactly what CODEOWNERS is for. It is not a reason to fork the work.
- The slot on `product-view` has no value without its consumer, and the consumer has no mount point without the slot.

**AGENTS.md Hard Rule 10** (never touch more than one protection tier without confirming scope) is satisfied by the brief itself: the tier split is enumerated and the manifest is fixed. The Tier 2 file must still be named in the commit body and PR body.

**How much loop this warrants — and what I am deliberately dropping.**

| Step | Loop depth | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — slot | **Light**: implement → `tsc` + `test` + diff review. No Tester/Scorer cycle. | Purely mechanical, behaviour-preserving-by-construction. The only failure mode (accidental non-verbatim edit) is caught by reading the diff, not by a test. |
| 2 — atom | **Full loop**: implement → Tester → Scorer, one revision cycle budgeted. | Real branching (selected / focusable / link-vs-static), real recipe, three guard suites to satisfy. |
| 3 — molecule | **Full loop**, one revision cycle budgeted. | Carries AC 1, AC 3 and AC 5 as branch logic plus roving-focus keyboard behaviour. Highest defect density in the story. |
| 4 — wiring | **Light**: implement → `tsc` + `test` + `audit:tokens` + developer visual check. | ~15 lines of prop mapping. The behaviour it produces is proven by steps 2 and 3; what is left is integration, which only a real PDP can prove. |

4. **Does the design intend the "Colour: <name>" label to persist in the multi-colour case?** AC 1 specifies it only for the single-colour case; ACs 2/3 are silent. **Interim default:** keep it in both cases — that is today's base behaviour, it is the smaller behavioural delta, and the container's 104px height (72px swatch + ~32px) is consistent with a label row. Confirm against `40001992:51881` during the Step 3 Figma read; if the container has no label row, this flips and the group renders swatches only in the multi-colour branch.

---

## 7. Assumptions (recorded, not blocking)

- **PDP uses the Large 48×72 variant.** Derived, not asked: the placement node `40000307:14062` puts the instance at 218×104, and 104 is the Large container's height (Small is 56).
- **Filter-then-count.** AC 5's "not surfaced to the shopper" resolves the interaction with AC 1: a 3-colour product with 1 populated image renders the text-label branch.
- **Zero populated colours** falls back to the text label for the selected colour rather than rendering nothing — the shopper still needs to know which colour they are viewing, and the colour *name* is product data, not image data.
- **Colour renders above size** because SFCC returns `variationAttributes` in that order. The slot preserves whatever order the API gives; it does not reorder. Verified visually in Step 4, not asserted in code.
- **`href` is always populated on the PDP path.** `useVariationAttributes` returns `href: null` only in controlled mode, and `product-detail`'s main `<ProductView>` passes no `controlledVariationValues`. The atom still handles the `href`-absent case so Storybook, Vitest and any future controlled caller work.
- **No E2E coverage for AC 4.** Stated in the Scale call. Raise a follow-up for a `pdp`-area Playwright spec plus the matching allow-list group in `qa.yml`'s `detect-changes`, without which any new `pdp` spec resolves to `e2e_scope: skip`.

---

## 8. Commit breakdown

Conventional commits (enforced by `scripts/hooks/commit-msg`). No Claude or CodeRabbit attribution in any message.

**1.**
```
feat(product-view): add renderVariationAttribute slot for per-attribute rendering

Adds one optional prop so a caller can replace the rendering of a single variation
attribute, leaving the others on the base markup. Mirrors the renderHeader slot added
in 227171e: type on ProductViewProps, fall-through at the call site, base body moved
verbatim into the default.

The slot is per-attribute rather than per-block deliberately. product-view renders
colour and size through the same loop and the same base SwatchGroup, distinguished only
by variant={id === 'color' ? 'circle' : 'square'}. A whole-block slot would pull the
size selector — which has its own separate Figma design and its own story — into a
colour-only change.

Fall-through is on undefined. Returning null also falls through and is not a way to
render nothing; documented on the prop.

The file header's claim of "exactly one additive optional prop" is corrected to name
both. No other change: no reformatting, no comment removal, no type tightening.

Refs SFCC-91
```

**2.**
```
feat(ui-kits): add ZimmColourSwatch atom

A single colour swatch: the variation's index image in a 48x72 box, rendered as a
react-router Link when an href is supplied so selection updates the URL without a
document load.

Height comes from aspectRatio 2/3 on var(--zimm-scale-1200) rather than a 72px literal
— no --zimm-* token exists at 72px and theme/foundation/ is Tier 1.

Does not carry base product-view's backgroundColor={name.toLowerCase()}. That tints
behind a missing image using the colour's display name as a CSS keyword ("Ivory"
resolves, "Bay Blue" does not); this component is only rendered for variations that
have an index image, so there is nothing to tint. A test pins the absence.

Recipe key is namespaced ZimmColourSwatch — an unnamespaced key would deep-merge the
base SFCC recipe (recipeGuards.test.ts).

Touches TIER 2 overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts (two lines: one import, one key)
to register the recipe. The recipe, the component and the registration are one commit
because recipeParts.test.ts fails on a recipe with no sibling index.tsx.

Refs SFCC-91
```

**3.**
```
feat(ui-kits): add ZimmColourSwatchGroup molecule

Renders the PDP colour picker. Multiple populated colours render as swatches with the
current one indicated (AC 2, AC 3); one colour renders as the text label "Colour: Bay
Blue" with no swatches (AC 1); a variation whose index image is not populated is
filtered out before either branch and is never surfaced (AC 5).

AC 5 is content population, not stock availability — a distinct condition from base
product-view's disabled={!orderable}, and a filtered variation is not rendered disabled,
it is not rendered at all. The filter lives here rather than on the PDP page so the
behaviour is provable from this component's own folder.

Roving tabindex and arrow-key focus movement match base swatch-group, so the group
remains a single tab stop.

Takes all data as props; useIntl only, per the components.md exemption. No swatch-group,
image-gallery, hook or translations change.

Touches TIER 2 overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts (two lines) to register the
recipe, in the same commit as the recipe for the reason given in the previous commit.

Refs SFCC-91
```

**4.**
```
feat(pdp): render colour variations through ZimmColourSwatchGroup

Passes renderVariationAttribute to the main ProductView, handling id === 'color' and
returning undefined for everything else so size falls through to the base rendering
unchanged. Resolves each variation's swatch image URL (disBaseLink || link) at the page
so the ui-kit components hold no SFCC shape knowledge.

The attribute id stays "color": Australian spelling applies to Zimmermann-authored
identifiers, not to SFCC attribute ids.

Set and bundle child ProductView instances are untouched.

Refs SFCC-91
```

# SFCC-91 — Build plan

**Story:** PDP UI — Colour Swatches & Variation Selection
**Branch:** `feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches` (deliberately not the other developer's branch name)
**Baseline:** `develop` @ `269d5d4` — `tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run test` 26 files / 408 tests green
**Architecture:** per-attribute render slot on `product-view`. Decided by Marcel 2026-08-31. Not revisited.

---

## 1. Goal

Build SFCC-91 to the five Jira ACs and the Figma `pdp/product-colour-picker` design, using a new
namespaced theme recipe plus a new atom and molecule under `ui-kits/`, consumed through a new
per-attribute render slot on the already-overridden `product-view` — with zero change to
`swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `translations/`, `theme/foundation/`, or any hook.

## 2. Scale — one branch, four commits

The three modified files cannot be usefully separated. The theme registration is 4 lines and would
otherwise register recipes that don't exist; the slot has no value without its consumer, and the
consumer has no mount point without the slot. Two code-owner teams on one PR is normal and is what
CODEOWNERS is for.

Hard Rule 10 (more than one protection tier) is satisfied by the manifest being fixed and
enumerated up front. The Tier 2 file must still be named in the commit body and the PR body.

| Step | Loop depth | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — slot | Light: implement → `tsc`/`lint`/`test` → diff review | Mechanical, behaviour-preserving by construction. Its one failure mode (a non-verbatim edit) is caught by reading the diff, not a test. |
| 2 — atom | Full loop, one revision cycle | Real branching, a new recipe, three guard suites. |
| 3 — molecule | Full loop, one revision cycle | Carries AC 1, 3 and 5 as branch logic plus roving focus. Highest defect density. |
| 4 — wiring | Light + developer visual check | ~15 lines of prop mapping; the behaviour is proven by 2 and 3. |

**Dropped deliberately:** no `.feature`/Playwright spec. `testing.md`'s gherkin workflow needs Lead
QA sign-off first, and `pdp` has no allow-list group in `qa.yml`'s `detect-changes`, so a new spec
would resolve to `e2e_scope: skip` and never run pre-merge. **AC 4 (no full page reload) is
genuinely an E2E assertion — this is a real coverage gap, not a free skip.** Raise as a follow-up.

## 3. File manifest

**Create — 8 new files**

| File | Tier | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx,index.test.tsx}` | 3 | squad-a + squad-b (`CODEOWNERS:176`) |
| `ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` | 3 | squad-a + squad-b (`:186` `**/*.css.ts` overrides `:176`; not the Tier 2 designer gate) |
| `ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx,index.test.tsx}` | 3 | squad-a + squad-b (`:176`) |
| `ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts` | 3 | squad-a + squad-b (`:186`) |

**Modify — exactly 3**

| File | Tier | Owner | Edit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` | **TIER 2** | tier-2 + tier-1 approvers (`:117`) | 2 imports + 2 keys. **Name in the commit and PR body.** |
| `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` | 4 — absent from both tier files **and** from CODEOWNERS | none | One optional prop + default + call site + header doc fix. Nothing else. |
| `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` | 3 | `pwa-squad-b` (`:162`) | Pass the slot on the main `<ProductView>` only. |

`.claude/registry/*.md` will be rewritten by the PostToolUse hook. Stage it; never hand-edit.

**Excluded, absolute:** `theme/foundation/**` (Tier 1), `swatch-group/`, `image-gallery/`,
`translations/`, `static/translations/`, `.storybook/**`, `hooks/**`.

## 4. Steps

### Pre-flight (not a commit)

```
git branch --show-current            # must not be develop/main
git checkout -b feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches
npm run audit:tokens > /tmp/audit-before.txt
```

Record the baseline count (~14 known pre-existing). Every later criterion is **"no new findings vs
baseline"**, never "zero findings".

### Step 1 — `renderVariationAttribute` slot on `product-view`

1. **Prop type** after `renderHeader` (~line 178):
   `renderVariationAttribute?: (attr: SfccVariationAttribute) => React.ReactNode;`
   JSDoc must state the fall-through contract: **return `undefined` to fall through to base
   rendering. Returning `null` also falls through and is not a way to render nothing** (`??` only
   tests nullish). A real trap — document it rather than let it be discovered.
2. **Extract the current loop body verbatim** into `const renderDefaultVariationAttribute = (attr) => {...}`
   declared inside the component body above the `return (` (~688). It must be inside the component
   because it closes over `intl` and `onVariationChange`. The body — `swatches` map, the
   `backgroundColor={name.toLowerCase()}` line, both `audit-allow` comments, `<Swatch>`,
   `<SwatchGroup>` — moves **byte-for-byte**. The destructure relocating from map params into the
   function body is the entire textual delta.
3. **No default at the destructure.** Unlike `renderHeader` it can't be expressed in the parameter
   list; the prop stays `undefined` and the call site handles fall-through.
4. **Call site** replaces the `variationAttributes.map(...)`:
   ```tsx
   variationAttributes.map((attr: SfccVariationAttribute) => (
     <React.Fragment key={attr.id}>
       {renderVariationAttribute?.(attr) ?? renderDefaultVariationAttribute(attr)}
     </React.Fragment>
   ))
   ```
   Use `React.Fragment` off the existing default import — do not add `Fragment` to the named list.
   A keyed Fragment emits no DOM, so output is byte-identical.
5. **Correct the file header (lines 19-21).** It asserts *"exactly one additive optional prop…
   `renderHeader`"*, which this change makes false. Name both, repeating the same three-part
   justification.

**Pass criteria** — `tsc`/`lint`/`test` all exit 0 · diff shows exactly one file · changed lines
< 90 · zero changes outside the four named regions (no reformatting, no comment deletion, no type
tightening) · `backgroundColor={name.toLowerCase()}` still present exactly once with its
`audit-allow` comment · `grep -c 'exactly one additive optional prop'` → 0 ·
`grep -rn "renderVariationAttribute" node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` → no hits.

### Step 2 — `ZimmColourSwatch` atom

Scaffold with `/new-component`; mirror `ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductStyleCode/`.

**Non-obvious sequencing constraint.** Recipe, component and registration land in **one commit**.
`recipeParts.test.ts` walks `overrides/app/components/**` for `*.css.ts` and asserts a sibling
`index.tsx` exists for any recipe declaring `parts:`. A commit with an orphan `.css.ts` **fails
`npm run test`**. Author in order: recipe → registration → component.

**Required Figma read first** — `40000307:13826` (Unselected), `40000307:13831` (Selected),
`40002689:3839` (Focus). Record border width, border colour, outline/offset, inner inset. Map each:

| Value | Token |
|---|---|
| 48px width | `var(--zimm-scale-1200)` — exists |
| 72px height | **no token exists** (gap between `1600`=64 and `3500`=140). Do not add one — Tier 1. Express as `aspectRatio: '2 / 3'` on the 48px width: yields exactly 72px, no raw unit, passes `audit:tokens`. |
| border width | `var(--zimm-border-width-default)` |
| border / selected | `var(--zimm-color-border-default)` / `-secondary` / `-focus` |
| focus ring | `var(--zimm-focus-ring)` + `var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)` |

**Any Figma value with no matching token: STOP and ask.** No invented hex, no `foundation/` edit.

**Recipe** — export `ZimmColourSwatch`; `parts: ['swatch','image']` (selected indicator on the
outer box so it doesn't scale or clip the image); `baseStyle` may be a function of `{selected}` —
safe, because `recipeGuards.test.ts:248-261` always invokes it with an object and walks both
branches. All colour/space as `var(--zimm-*)`.

**Component** — props `{name, imageUrl, href?, isSelected, isFocusable}`.
`useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmColourSwatch', {selected: isSelected})` above any early return.
`const ColourSwatchLink = chakra(RouteLink)` using `Link` from `react-router-dom` — the same import
base `swatch.jsx:16` uses. **This is what delivers AC 4**: a router Link pushes history without a
document load. No `overrides/.../link` component exists.
Render `role="radio"`, `aria-checked`, `aria-label={name}`, `tabIndex={isFocusable ? 0 : -1}`.
The dynamic image URL cannot live in the recipe, so it goes on the element as
`__css={{...styles.image, backgroundImage: `url(${imageUrl})`}}` — the one legitimate dynamic
spread, exactly the shape `footer/footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44,62` already uses.
Falls back to a non-link `chakra.span` when `href` is absent.
**Deliberate divergence from base line 797:** no `backgroundColor={name.toLowerCase()}`. Comment
the reason — (a) it's a CSS keyword coincidence, not a token ("Ivory" resolves, "Bay Blue" doesn't),
unauditable and against `css.md`; (b) it exists to tint behind a *missing* image and AC 5 guarantees
this component never renders without one; (c) `background-size: cover` hides it anyway. Base keeps
it; size still routes through the untouched path.

**Story** — `Commerce/ZimmColourSwatch`; `Default`, `Selected`, `WithoutLink`. **Must add a local
`MemoryRouter` decorator** — `.storybook/preview.tsx` supplies Chakra and Intl only, no router, and
`.storybook/` is Tier 1 so no global decorator is available.

**Test** — wrap in `MemoryRouter`. Assert only this atom's contract: href present → anchor with
that href; href absent → no anchor, still `role="radio"`; `aria-checked` both ways; `tabIndex` 0
vs -1; the resolved URL appears in `background-image`; and a **regression guard** that rendering
with `name="Bay Blue"` leaves `element.style.backgroundColor === ''`.

**Pass criteria** — `tsc`/`lint`/`test`/`audit:tokens` clean, count == baseline ·
`recipeParts.test.ts` output shows a `zimmColourSwatch` case (proves collected, not skipped) ·
`grep -c "ZimmColourSwatch" overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` → 2 ·
raw-value grep on the `.css.ts` returns nothing · no `sx=` in `index.tsx` ·
**mutation check:** flip `aria-checked` to a constant `true`, confirm the selected-state test
fails, revert. A criterion never made to fail does not count.

### Step 3 — `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` molecule

Same one-commit orphan-recipe constraint.

**Required Figma read first** — `40001992:51881` (Colour Options, `Type=Large` 192×104): layout
mode, `itemSpacing`, padding, and whether a label row occupies the ~32px above the 72px swatch row.
Map to `var(--zimm-scale-*)`. **No matching token → STOP and ask.**

**Recipe** — export `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`; `parts: ['root','label','labelName','swatches']`.
Any responsive step is an **explicit media query** off `BP` in `theme/components/footerShared.ts` —
never Chakra's array shorthand, which fails the bare-token guard at every element.

**Props** — `{label, selectedName?, selectedValue?, values: readonly ZimmColourSwatchValue[]}`
where a value is `{value, name, href?, imageUrl?}` and `imageUrl: undefined` means the index image
is not populated.

**The three ACs that live here as branch logic:**
- **AC 5 — filter, and it belongs here.** `values.filter(v => Boolean(v.imageUrl))`. This is
  *content population*, structurally distinct from base's `disabled={!orderable}` (*stock
  availability*) at `product-view:817`. A filtered variation is not rendered disabled — it is not
  rendered at all. It lives in the molecule, not the page, because `testing.md` requires a
  component's contract to be provable from its own folder and the 999-line PDP page has no test.
- **AC 1** — `populated.length <= 1` renders the label line only, no `swatches` node. Filter first,
  then count: AC 5 says an unpopulated variation isn't surfaced, so counting it toward "multiple
  colours" would violate it.
- **AC 2/3** — one `<ZimmColourSwatch>` per populated value; `isSelected = value === selectedValue`;
  `isFocusable = isSelected || (!selectedValue && index === 0)` — base's exact roving rule.

**Label** — `const intl = useIntl()` (never destructured). Reuse base's own message id
`swatch_group.selected.label`, `defaultMessage: '{label}:'`. `useIntl` in a leaf is explicitly
exempted by `components.md`. No `translations/*.json` edit.

**Keyboard** — `role="radiogroup"` + `aria-label`; `onKeyDown` moving focus across children with
arrows, mirroring base `swatch-group/index.jsx`. Arrows move **focus only**, not navigation — which
matches live behaviour today, since `product-detail` passes no `onVariationChange` so base's
`handleChange` is already `noop`. Activation is the anchor's native Enter. Space does not activate
an anchor — record as an inherited parity gap in a comment, not a new regression.

**Story** — `Commerce/ZimmColourSwatchGroup`, local `MemoryRouter`. `Default` (4 populated, one
selected), `SingleColour`, `WithUnpopulatedVariations` (5 values, 2 without `imageUrl`),
`NoneSelected`. A `play` on `Default` asserting arrow-key focus movement.

**Test** — `MemoryRouter` + `IntlProvider` (the latter because `useIntl` throws without one).
Seven assertions: one colour → 0 radios and text reads `Colour: Bay Blue`; three colours → 3 radios;
exactly one `aria-checked="true"` matching `selectedName`; **AC 5** 5 values / 2 unpopulated → 3
radios and neither excluded name in `container.textContent`; **AC 5 vs orderability** a value with
`imageUrl` renders regardless of stock signal, proving the filter keys on image; AC 5 reducing 3
colours to 1 populated triggers the AC 1 branch; exactly one element with `tabIndex === 0`.

**Pass criteria** — `tsc`/`lint`/`test`/`audit:tokens` clean vs baseline · `recipeParts` shows a
passing `zimmColourSwatchGroup` case · no Chakra responsive arrays in the recipe · no data-fetching
hook imported in the leaf · `var(--zimm` in `index.tsx` only from the dynamic `backgroundImage`
spread, if at all · **mutation check:** delete the `imageUrl` filter, confirm the AC 5 test fails,
restore.

### Step 4 — Wire the slot on the PDP

On the **main `<ProductView>` at ~line 891 only** — not the set/bundle instances at ~801 and ~827,
which are child products in a different layout and out of scope.

```tsx
renderVariationAttribute={(attr) =>
  attr.id === 'color' ? (
    <ZimmColourSwatchGroup
      label={attr.name}
      selectedName={attr.selectedValue?.name}
      selectedValue={attr.selectedValue?.value}
      values={attr.values.map((v) => ({
        value: v.value, name: v.name, href: v.href,
        imageUrl: v.image?.disBaseLink || v.image?.link,
      }))}
    />
  ) : undefined
}
```

`undefined`, not `null`, for non-colour — `null` also falls through today, but `undefined` is the
documented sentinel. `attr.id === 'color'` stays US-spelled: Australian spelling applies to
Zimmermann-authored identifiers, not SFCC attribute ids. URL resolution happens here so the ui-kit
components carry no SFCC shape knowledge — mirroring `getVariantValueSwatch`, which returns
`undefined` when no `viewType: 'swatch'` group matches, the exact condition AC 5 describes.
**No hook is wrapped, overridden or modified.**

**Pass criteria** — `tsc`/`lint`/`test`/`audit:tokens` clean · diff touches only the import block
and the single `<ProductView>` · `grep -c "renderVariationAttribute"` → 1 ·
`npm run test:max-file-size` not required (it triggers a full build); note in the PR that this adds
two small components and no new dependency.

**Developer visual verification** — do **not** run `npm start` (AGENTS.md). Ask Marcel to check on
his running dev server, on a real multi-colour PDP:
1. colour renders as image swatches, size still renders as base squares, colour above size;
2. clicking a swatch changes the URL and there is no white flash — Network shows no top-level
   document request;
3. the selected swatch is visually indicated;
4. a single-colour PDP shows `Colour: <name>` with no swatches;
5. Tab reaches the group once, arrows move focus within it, Enter navigates.

## 5. Loop configuration

| Step | Tester | Scorer PASS |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `tsc`/`lint`/`test`; diff-review the moved body against `git show HEAD:…` lines 785-847; confirm both `audit-allow` comments survived, `backgroundColor` present once, header names two props | All green **and** diff confined to the four regions **and** < 90 changed lines **and** the stale header sentence gone. Any reformatting or comment removal outside those regions is **FAIL even if tests pass**. |
| 2 | Above + `audit:tokens`; confirm `recipeParts` lists a `zimmColourSwatch` case; raw-value grep; `aria-checked` mutation | All green; `audit:tokens` == baseline; raw-value grep empty; the mutation makes a test fail. **FAIL if** the key is not `ZimmColourSwatch`, **or** a name-derived `backgroundColor` appears, **or** the story lacks `MemoryRouter` (it would throw on open while Vitest still passes). |
| 3 | Above + no-data-hooks grep, responsive-array grep, `imageUrl`-filter mutation, all 7 assertions present | All green. **FAIL if** AC 5 is implemented as `orderable`-based rather than image-based, **or** the AC 1 branch still renders a `radiogroup` with one radio, **or** the filter was pushed up into the PDP page. |
| 4 | `tsc`/`lint`/`test`/`audit:tokens`; diff confined; set/bundle instances untouched; then hand the five-point checklist to Marcel | **PASS-pending-developer-confirmation**, not PASS. The Tester cannot verify AC 4's no-reload behaviour from a terminal and must not claim it. Scorer must not close this step on green tests alone. |

**Budget:** one revision cycle each for steps 2 and 3. A third cycle means a missing Figma value or
a wrong architectural read — stop and escalate rather than iterate.

## 6. Open questions

1. **`>4 colours` overflow.** `40001992:51881` is described as the ">4 colours" design, but at
   192×104 it fits one row of 72px swatches with ~32px of label — it cannot wrap at that height.
   Six colours: horizontal scroll, wrap with the container growing, or a "+N" affordance? No AC
   covers it. **Interim default:** `flexWrap: 'wrap'`, container grows; tests assert nothing about
   overflow; called out in the PR as unresolved.
2. **Does BM return "Colour" or "Color" as the attribute display name on AU?** AC 1's example is
   `"Colour: Bay Blue"`, and the label comes from `attr.name` — BM data. If BM returns "Color" we
   render "Color: Bay Blue" and miss the AC's literal example. Hardcoding "Colour" would break the
   other ten locales and is not an option. Needs the BM attribute owner.
3. **Is `Small/Rounded` 20×24 needed, and where does its corner radius come from?** There is **no
   border-radius token anywhere in `theme/foundation/`** (no `radius` key in `zimmTokens.ts`,
   `spacing.ts` or `sizes.ts`). Building it needs either a Tier 1 addition (excluded, absolute) or
   an unapproved raw value, and it has no PDP consumer. **Decision: excluded from this story**, with
   the reason recorded in the recipe. If the designer intends it for PLP/quick-view it needs its own
   ticket *and* a foundation radius token first.
4. **Does the "Colour: <name>" label persist in the multi-colour case?** AC 1 specifies it only for
   the single-colour case; ACs 2/3 are silent. **Interim default:** keep it in both — smaller
   behavioural delta from base, and the 104px container height (72 + ~32) is consistent with a label
   row. Confirm during the Step 3 Figma read; if there's no label row, this flips.

## 7. Assumptions

- **PDP uses the Large 48×72 variant** — derived from the placement node being 218×104, and 104 is
  the Large container height (Small is 56). Not confirmed by anyone.
- **Filter-then-count** — a 3-colour product with 1 populated image renders the AC 1 text branch.
- **Zero populated colours** falls back to the text label for the selected colour rather than
  rendering nothing: the shopper still needs to know what they're viewing, and the colour *name* is
  product data, not image data.
- **Colour renders above size** because SFCC returns `variationAttributes` in that order. The slot
  preserves API order and does not reorder. Verified visually in Step 4, not asserted in code.
- **`href` is always populated on the PDP path** — `useVariationAttributes` returns `href: null`
  only in controlled mode, and the main `<ProductView>` passes no `controlledVariationValues`. The
  atom still handles the absent case for Storybook, Vitest and any future controlled caller.

## PreBuild complete — SFCC-91

**The gate is clear. No 🔴 remain.** Plan and findings are at `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-91/`. Repo untouched throughout — `git status` clean.

### One thing worth leading with

The last check I ran overturned a decision the plan had already made. The planner, reasoning from the container being 192×104, concluded the ">4 colours" design couldn't wrap and defaulted to `flexWrap: 'wrap'`.

I read the node instead of reasoning about it. Both variants contain a **`Pagination` frame with left/right chevrons** above a fixed **four-swatch window**. The >4 treatment is **pagination**, not wrapping. That default would have shipped the wrong behaviour and it would have looked correct in review.

The icon dependency is already satisfied — `ChevronLeftIcon` / `ChevronRightIcon` exist in `overrides/app/components/icons/zimm.tsx`, Zimmermann-drawn from Figma. Step 3 now carries the pagination controls, their a11y, and a `ZimmIcon` mock in its Vitest test.

### The plan

**One branch, four commits.** `feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches`.

| | Count | Tier exposure |
|---|---|---|
| New files | 8 | All Tier 3, squad-a + squad-b |
| Modified | 3 | **1 × Tier 2** (`theme/components/index.ts`), 1 × Tier 3 (`product-detail`, squad-b), 1 × unowned (`product-view` — in neither tier file nor CODEOWNERS) |

Steps 2 and 3 run the full implementer→tester→scorer loop with one revision cycle budgeted; steps 1 and 4 are single-pass with a diff review. A third cycle on 2 or 3 means a missing Figma value or a wrong architectural read — stop, don't iterate.

**Two constraints the planner found that I'd missed:**
- `recipeParts.test.ts` fails on a recipe with no sibling `index.tsx`, so recipe + component + registration must land in **one commit**, not three.
- **There is no border-radius token anywhere in `theme/foundation/`.** The `Small/Rounded` variant can't be built without a Tier 1 addition, and it has no PDP consumer — so it's excluded, with the reason recorded in the recipe. That's a scope reduction against a designed variant; your call whether to accept it.
- Also neat: 72px has no token either (gap between 64 and 140), so height comes from `aspectRatio: '2 / 3'` on the 48px token rather than a raw literal. Passes `audit:tokens` cleanly.

### Still open — carried as stated assumptions, not resolved

1. **Does BM return "Colour" or "Color"** as the attribute display name on AU? AC 1's example is "Colour: Bay Blue" and the label comes from BM data. Hardcoding "Colour" would break the other ten locales, so this needs the attribute owner, not a code fix.
2. **Does the "Colour: `<name>`" label persist in the multi-colour case?** AC 1 specifies it only for single-colour. Default is to keep it; confirmed during the Step 3 Figma read.
3. **`viewType: 'swatch'` vs the index image** — still the one that decides whether this is a styling story or a data story.
4. **AC 4 has no automated coverage.** No-full-reload is genuinely an E2E assertion, and a new `pdp` spec would hit `e2e_scope: skip` because `qa.yml` has no `pdp` allow-list group. Step 4 is explicitly **PASS-pending-your-visual-confirmation**, not PASS — the tester is instructed not to claim it from a terminal.

### Ready for Build

Baseline is green (408 tests, `tsc` clean), so anything red afterwards is Build's doing. Two things before you invoke it: you're on `develop`, so a branch is needed first, and `zimmerMANNPreBuild` stops here by design — Build is your call, not mine.

content.text:
Yes — and it was worth doing. All three are now answered from live data rather than carried as assumptions.

## What the API said

**1. BM returns "Colour", not "Color".** Product `8637DS241` on the dev tier returns:

```
variationAttributes[0]  id='color'   name='Colour'   values=1  → 'BLUBIR' / 'Blue Birds'
variationAttributes[1]  id='size'    name='Size'     values=6
```

So AC 1's literal *"Colour: Bay Blue"* falls straight out of `attr.name`. No hardcoding, no locale risk, no BM change. The SFCC key stays US-spelled `color` — exactly the split the plan already assumed.

**2. `viewType: 'swatch'` exists and is populated — and this is a styling story, not a data story.** But the mechanism has a catch worth knowing:

| Request | imageGroups | `swatch` groups |
|---|---|---|
| without `allImages` | 4 | 1 — **no `variationAttributes`** |
| `allImages=true` | 8 | 2 — one carrying `variationAttributes: color=['BLUBIR']` |

Base `getVariantValueSwatch` filters on `viewType:'swatch'` **and** `variationValues:{color: value}`. That second condition only matches the group that appears **when `allImages=true`**. Without the flag, every colour's `image` comes back `undefined` — and under the plan's AC 5 filter, *no swatches would render at all*.

The PDP already passes it: `product-detail/index.tsx:220`, on the main `useProduct`. (The `allImages: false` at `:282` is the set/bundle child fetch, already out of scope.) So no fetch change is needed, and SFCC-91 adds no new exposure to the `allImages` behaviour recorded under SFCC-29 — it's already how the PDP loads.

Standing risk now noted in the plan: flip `:220` to `false` and every swatch silently vanishes. That deserves an inline comment at the call site.

**3. The label persists in the multi-colour case** — answered from Figma, not API. `40000307:13867`'s `labelContainer` holds a `Label group` with **two text nodes** (36px + 96px — "Colour:" and the value) next to `Pagination`, sitting directly above the four-swatch row. So it's present in the multi-colour design too.

And `Small/Rounded` is recorded as out of scope per your call, with the no-radius-token reason kept in the recipe so it isn't rediscovered later.

## One honest limitation

The dev catalogue has exactly **one** searchable product, with **one** colour. So I've verified the *mechanism* end to end, but multi-colour rendering, pagination past four, and AC 5's unpopulated case have not been exercised against real data — only fixtures will cover them until Step 4 runs against a richer tier. That's stated in the plan rather than glossed.

**Net effect on the gate:** the last 🟡 is closed. Findings now reads ✅ CLEAR; three of the four open questions are answered and the fourth is your accepted scope cut. What remains is the known AC 4 coverage gap — no automated no-reload assertion, deliberately, because a new `pdp` spec would hit `e2e_scope: skip`.

Plan and findings are current at `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-91/`. Repo still untouched. Ready for Build when you are — you're on `develop`, so it needs a branch first.

Housekeeping done — three of those were stale and are now closed. Here's the honest state.

## Nothing blocks Build. But three things are worth your call first.

**1. The story got bigger after you last saw the plan.** When I verified the ">4 colours" node, I found chevron **pagination** — a fixed four-swatch window with prev/next. That's design-mandated, not optional, but it adds windowing state, two controls, their a11y, a `ZimmIcon` dependency, and a Vitest icon mock to Step 3. The molecule is now the largest piece of the story, not the atom.

**2. The plan deliberately drops a base behaviour.** Base line 797 sets `backgroundColor={name.toLowerCase()}` behind the swatch image — using the colour's display name as a raw CSS keyword. The new component omits it, on the grounds that it only tints behind a *missing* image and AC 5 guarantees this component never renders without one. I think that's right, and there's a test pinning the absence so it survives refactoring. But it is a deliberate divergence from base and it will show up in review, so it should be your call rather than the planner's.

**3. Step 4's visual check has nowhere good to run.** The dev catalogue has exactly one searchable product, with one colour. Multi-colour, pagination past four, and AC 5's unpopulated case can't be seen there — only in Storybook fixtures. You'll need a richer tier for the five-point check.

## Two follow-ups to log — outside this story

- **The PRDs still say don't build this.** You ruled SPR-26 stale, but `.docs/prd/plp.md` §5.4 and `pdp.md:219` still read *"Do not implement until confirmed."* The zimmerMANN skills are barred from writing to `.docs/prd/**`, so that correction needs a human. Worth doing before the next person hits the same stop.
- **AC 4 has no automated coverage.** A `pdp` Playwright spec needs a Lead QA-signed `.feature` *and* a `pdp` allow-list group in `qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` — the latter is Tier 1 CI config. Separate ticket.

## Two facts, no decision needed

CODEOWNERS will request **Squad B** review regardless of the `Squad-A` label. And the design tracker records PDP components frozen 13 Aug under a no-changes rule while design was still pending on the 26th — process drift worth raising, not a build blocker.

content.text:
Verified — and the answer is "yes, but not here." Let me lay it out.

**Intent: yes.** PRD-004 says the system displays *"Also available in" / "Only available in"* colour swatches, and SFCC-708's own description is explicit — products with different style codes *"can be associated and appear as selectable colour swatches on each other's PDP."* So cross-SKU colours belong in the same swatch row.

**But they can't be built in SFCC-91.** I checked the live product payload: the only custom attributes on a product today are `c_careInstructions` and `c_sizeFit`. There is **no related-colours attribute** — which is exactly why Jasmijn moved that AC out to SFCC-708 on 12 Aug ("needs a BM product attribute that doesn't exist yet"). SFCC-708 is Ready for Development, unstarted, with Victor on it.

**The good news on wiring — the plan already anticipates this.** The molecule doesn't take SFCC's `attr`. It takes a normalised array:

```ts
values: readonly { value, name, href?, imageUrl? }[]
```

with the SFCC→prop mapping done at the page in Step 4. So SFCC-708 appends related products to that array at the page level and the molecule renders them with **no change**. That's not luck — it's the container/presentational rule in `components.md` doing its job.

**Two real gaps your question exposes, though:**

1. **The label is undesigned for this case.** PRD-004 implies the group label changes to *"Also available in"* / *"Only available in"*. The Figma `labelContainer` shows two text nodes sizing to `"Colour:"` + value — matching AC 1, with no "Also available in" variant anywhere. So if related colours need a different label, that's a design gap, not an implementation detail.

2. **Same-master and cross-product swatches behave differently.** A same-master swatch is a variant switch (AC 4: no reload). A cross-product one is a navigation to a different PDP. Right now both would render as an identical `RouteLink` and the molecule couldn't tell them apart.

content.content:
---
name: zimmerMANNBuild
description: The builder. Executes an approved zimmerMANNPreBuild plan through a closed-loop multi-agent workflow — implement, test, scope-check, score, rework until passed — committing each step and handing off to zimmerMANNPostBuild. Also handles rework from CodeRabbit or reviewer change requests after a PR is open.
---

The executor. Takes an approved plan and builds it, one step at a time, with every step tested,
scope-checked, scored and seen by Marcel before it becomes a commit.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — the loop
agents are pinned to Sonnet in their own frontmatter regardless.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full loop. The plan states the scale it
chose and why; honour it. Over-scaled machinery is a defect, not thoroughness. Nothing too crazy,
no overthinking.

---

## Two modes

**`build`** — `$ARGUMENTS` is a Jira key. Reads `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`
and executes it. This is the default.

**`rework`** — invoked as `rework <TICKET>` after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has
requested changes. Skips planning entirely; see the last section.

If no plan exists for the ticket, stop and say so. **Do not plan here** — that is
`zimmerMANNPreBuild`'s job, and building from an unplanned story is how an afternoon gets burned
on the wrong thing.

---

## Before the first step

1. Confirm the branch. **Not `develop`, not `main`** — a `PreToolUse` hook blocks every Write and
   Edit there. If the branch is wrong, stop.
2. Confirm the working tree is clean, or that everything dirty is expected and belongs to this
   story. Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.
3. Read the plan's file manifest, tiers and per-step pass criteria. **Any file marked BLOCKED
   stops the run** until Marcel confirms owner approval.
4. Record the baseline: run the four per-step gates now and note the numbers. A gate that is
   non-zero at baseline is not a failure you introduced.

---

## The loop — once per step

```
Implementer  →  Tester  →  Orchestrator  →  Scorer  →  [Marcel]  →  commit
                   ↑                          │
                   └────── REWORK, max 3 ─────┘
```

**1. `zm-implementer`** builds the step. Only the files the step names. It never stages and never
commits.

**2. `zm-tester`** fans out its own angle sub-agents, re-pointed for this step, and reports
findings with CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE and UNIFORM/ONE-OFF labels, plus what it tried to falsify and
what it could not verify.

**3. `zm-orchestrator`** returns a scope verdict — IN SCOPE / UNDER / OVER / BLOCKED. Under and
over carry equal weight.

**4. `zm-scorer`** takes both and scores six axes. PASS or REWORK.

**REWORK returns to the Implementer with a specific instruction. Maximum three rounds.** On the
third, stop and surface to Marcel — three failures means the plan or the criteria are wrong, not
the implementation.

### Per-step gates — the cheap four

Run every step. Seconds each.

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test                        # includes recipeGuards, the hard styling gate
npm run lint                        # compare counts, not the exit code
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs    # new unacknowledged findings only
```

Two traps: `npm run lint` exits non-zero at a healthy baseline, so **compare the count against
your baseline and ignore the exit code**. And never append arguments to it — `pwa-kit-dev lint`
forwards `--`-args into `execSync`, which can silently turn the gate into a writer.

The plan's per-step pass criteria layer **on top of** these, they do not replace them.

### The visual checkpoint

**After any step that changes rendered output, the loop stops.** The plan marks which steps those
are; if it doesn't, assume any step touching a component, a recipe or a page does.

Tell Marcel exactly:
- the URL and the viewport to open
- the Figma node to compare against — the one for **that variant and state**
- what should be on screen
- what would indicate a defect, including anything that will look wrong but is correct

Then **wait.** Do not proceed on assumption. This is the only gate on this stack that catches a
layout defect — `width: 'xl'` passed every automated check and destroyed the global footer.

Until it has happened, the Scorer's Design fidelity axis is UNVERIFIED, not passed.

### The commit

**The skill commits, not an agent.** Only after: Scorer PASS, and the visual checkpoint passed if
one was owed.

One step, one commit. Conventional Commits — the `commit-msg` hook enforces it. **No Claude
attribution, no CodeRabbit mentions, no `Co-Authored-By` line.** Use Marcel's previously authored
commits on this repo as the reference for tone and body.

Then move to the next step.

---

## Before handing off

Once every step has passed, run the expensive gates **once**:

```
npm run build-storybook             # then run the interaction + a11y suite against it
npm run test:story                  # real BrowserStack, scoped to the Jira key
npm run test:max-file-size          # runs a full build
cr review --uncommitted             # CodeRabbit locally, before anything is public
```

Storybook needs a verified-free port and a build you can prove is yours — a stale server on 6006
produced a silently meaningless pass once. Check the served build matches your own before trusting
any result.

Then **write the handoff** to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/handoff.md`:

```
# Handoff — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Base: <sha>   Head: <sha>

## Steps
| # | What | Commit | Scorer verdict | Rework rounds |

## Gates (real numbers, not claims)
| Gate | Result | Baseline |

## UNIFORM findings
<each one, with file:line — these are what a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>

## Outstanding
<anything left, or "none">
```

**Write it even when everything passed.** PostBuild reads this file, and it may run in a different
session — a handoff that exists only in conversation does not survive the session ending.

Then present the same content to Marcel and **hand off to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`. This skill does
not push and does not open a PR.**

---

## Rework mode

Entered after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has requested changes.

**Read `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md` first.** It records what earlier rounds
already declined and why. A finding that was declined with evidence in round one does not get
re-litigated in round three — check before you verify anything, and if you disagree with a previous
decline, say so rather than silently reversing it.

**1. Verify every finding before touching anything.** CodeRabbit has been wrong on this repo
often — one batch ran 1-in-6 correct. Treat each finding as a hypothesis, not a fact. Per finding:

- **VALID** — reproduce it, cite `file:line`, fix it
- **INVALID** — say what is actually true, with the evidence, and draft the reply
- **OUT OF SCOPE** — real but not this story's problem; name the owning ticket or the person
- **DEFER** — real, in scope, but blocked on a decision; name who decides

**2. Fix only the VALID ones.** Same rules as build mode — the Implementer touches only what the
finding names, never stages, never commits.

**3. Re-run the cheap four**, plus the visual checkpoint if the fix changes rendered output.

**4. Commit the fixes here**, same rule as build mode — the skill commits, never an agent. Reference
the review thread each commit answers.

**5. Hand back to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`** with: what was fixed and in which commit, what was
declined and why, and the evidence behind each decline. **PostBuild owns the push and the
in-thread replies** — every finding gets a written answer, including the declined ones.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never push. Never open or update a PR.** That boundary belongs to PostBuild, which presents
  first and pushes only once Marcel has given the go.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never touch a Tier 1 file** without Marcel naming it and confirming owner approval.
- **Never expand scope.** Something worth doing that the plan didn't ask for gets reported, not
  done. Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Local-only docs are never citable** in a commit message or a code comment. Cite `AGENTS.md`
  or `.claude/rules/*` instead.
- **Say what you could not verify.** Silence reads as "nothing wrong" when it may mean
  "didn't look there".

content.text:
Straight answers to all three.

## 1. Is the plan fully built?

**Substantively yes** — goal, scale call, manifest with tiers, four sequenced steps with concrete criteria, seven logged decisions, assumptions, commit breakdown. Nothing about *what to build* is missing.

## 2. Ready to hand off?

**It wasn't when you asked.** Two real problems:

**A missing baseline.** Build's "before the first step" requires baselines for all four cheap gates. I'd captured `tsc`, `test` and `audit:tokens` — but not `lint`. Now done: **20 problems, 4 errors, 16 warnings, exit 1.** That matters because lint *fails at a healthy baseline*, so a step comparing exit codes would read green work as broken. All four errors are pre-existing Prettier issues in `routes.tsx` and `recipeGuards.test.ts`, none in our files.

## 3. Was it formatted for the closed-loop workflow?

**No — and this was the right question to ask.** Three concrete mismatches, all now fixed:

**The Orchestrator had no input at all.** The loop is Implementer → Tester → **Orchestrator** → Scorer, but my §5 table had columns only for Tester and Scorer. The Orchestrator's first check is *"every file in the diff is in the plan's manifest"* — and my manifest was **global**, not per-step. It literally could not do its job. There's now a per-step manifest: Step 1 permits exactly one file, Step 2 permits four plus the theme index, and so on. Anything else is an OVER finding.

**Visual checkpoints weren't marked.** Build says *"the plan marks which steps those are; if it doesn't, assume any step touching a component, a recipe or a page does"* — which silently makes all four stop, with no guidance on what to compare against. There's now a checkpoint table naming, per step: the surface, the exact Figma node for **that variant and state**, what should be on screen, and what indicates a defect. Step 1's is a *regression* check — it has no Figma node, because the correct outcome is that nothing visibly changes at all.

**The Scorer's six axes weren't addressed.** It scores Pass criteria / Correctness / Design fidelity / Conformance / Completeness / Restraint. My PASS conditions were ad-hoc prose, so the Scorer would have been reconciling two schemas. They're now mapped per step, axis by axis.

## One thing that fell out of the fix

Writing the checkpoint table forced the Step 4 problem into the open: **the dev catalogue has one product with one colour.** Multi-colour, pagination and AC 5 genuinely cannot be seen there. That's now written into the plan as an instruction to raise it with you rather than let a tester declare the checkpoint passed on a single-colour product — which is exactly how a green run means nothing.

Plan is 469 lines and now speaks the loop's language. **Ready for `zimmerMANNBuild` on `feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches`.**

Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNBuild

The executor. Takes an approved plan and builds it, one step at a time, with every step tested,
scope-checked, scored and seen by Marcel before it becomes a commit.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — the loop
agents are pinned to Sonnet in their own frontmatter regardless.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full loop. The plan states the scale it
chose and why; honour it. Over-scaled machinery is a defect, not thoroughness. Nothing too crazy,
no overthinking.

---

## Two modes

**`build`** — `- let's run the build` is a Jira key. Reads `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`
and executes it. This is the default.

**`rework`** — invoked as `rework <TICKET>` after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has
requested changes. Skips planning entirely; see the last section.

If no plan exists for the ticket, stop and say so. **Do not plan here** — that is
`zimmerMANNPreBuild`'s job, and building from an unplanned story is how an afternoon gets burned
on the wrong thing.

---

## Before the first step

1. Confirm the branch. **Not `develop`, not `main`** — a `PreToolUse` hook blocks every Write and
   Edit there. If the branch is wrong, stop.
2. Confirm the working tree is clean, or that everything dirty is expected and belongs to this
   story. Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.
3. Read the plan's file manifest, tiers and per-step pass criteria. **Any file marked BLOCKED
   stops the run** until Marcel confirms owner approval.
4. Record the baseline: run the four per-step gates now and note the numbers. A gate that is
   non-zero at baseline is not a failure you introduced.

---

## The loop — once per step

```
Implementer  →  Tester  →  Orchestrator  →  Scorer  →  [Marcel]  →  commit
                   ↑                          │
                   └────── REWORK, max 3 ─────┘
```

**1. `zm-implementer`** builds the step. Only the files the step names. It never stages and never
commits.

**2. `zm-tester`** fans out its own angle sub-agents, re-pointed for this step, and reports
findings with CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE and UNIFORM/ONE-OFF labels, plus what it tried to falsify and
what it could not verify.

**3. `zm-orchestrator`** returns a scope verdict — IN SCOPE / UNDER / OVER / BLOCKED. Under and
over carry equal weight.

**4. `zm-scorer`** takes both and scores six axes. PASS or REWORK.

**REWORK returns to the Implementer with a specific instruction. Maximum three rounds.** On the
third, stop and surface to Marcel — three failures means the plan or the criteria are wrong, not
the implementation.

### Per-step gates — the cheap four

Run every step. Seconds each.

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test                        # includes recipeGuards, the hard styling gate
npm run lint                        # compare counts, not the exit code
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs    # new unacknowledged findings only
```

Two traps: `npm run lint` exits non-zero at a healthy baseline, so **compare the count against
your baseline and ignore the exit code**. And never append arguments to it — `pwa-kit-dev lint`
forwards `--`-args into `execSync`, which can silently turn the gate into a writer.

The plan's per-step pass criteria layer **on top of** these, they do not replace them.

### The visual checkpoint

**After any step that changes rendered output, the loop stops.** The plan marks which steps those
are; if it doesn't, assume any step touching a component, a recipe or a page does.

Tell Marcel exactly:
- the URL and the viewport to open
- the Figma node to compare against — the one for **that variant and state**
- what should be on screen
- what would indicate a defect, including anything that will look wrong but is correct

Then **wait.** Do not proceed on assumption. This is the only gate on this stack that catches a
layout defect — `width: 'xl'` passed every automated check and destroyed the global footer.

Until it has happened, the Scorer's Design fidelity axis is UNVERIFIED, not passed.

### The commit

**The skill commits, not an agent.** Only after: Scorer PASS, and the visual checkpoint passed if
one was owed.

One step, one commit. Conventional Commits — the `commit-msg` hook enforces it. **No Claude
attribution, no CodeRabbit mentions, no `Co-Authored-By` line.** Use Marcel's previously authored
commits on this repo as the reference for tone and body.

Then move to the next step.

---

## Before handing off

Once every step has passed, run the expensive gates **once**:

```
npm run build-storybook             # then run the interaction + a11y suite against it
npm run test:story                  # real BrowserStack, scoped to the Jira key
npm run test:max-file-size          # runs a full build
cr review --uncommitted             # CodeRabbit locally, before anything is public
```

Storybook needs a verified-free port and a build you can prove is yours — a stale server on 6006
produced a silently meaningless pass once. Check the served build matches your own before trusting
any result.

Then **write the handoff** to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/handoff.md`:

```
# Handoff — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Base: <sha>   Head: <sha>

## Steps
| # | What | Commit | Scorer verdict | Rework rounds |

## Gates (real numbers, not claims)
| Gate | Result | Baseline |

## UNIFORM findings
<each one, with file:line — these are what a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>

## Outstanding
<anything left, or "none">
```

**Write it even when everything passed.** PostBuild reads this file, and it may run in a different
session — a handoff that exists only in conversation does not survive the session ending.

Then present the same content to Marcel and **hand off to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`. This skill does
not push and does not open a PR.**

---

## Rework mode

Entered after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has requested changes.

**Read `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md` first.** It records what earlier rounds
already declined and why. A finding that was declined with evidence in round one does not get
re-litigated in round three — check before you verify anything, and if you disagree with a previous
decline, say so rather than silently reversing it.

**1. Verify every finding before touching anything.** CodeRabbit has been wrong on this repo
often — one batch ran 1-in-6 correct. Treat each finding as a hypothesis, not a fact. Per finding:

- **VALID** — reproduce it, cite `file:line`, fix it
- **INVALID** — say what is actually true, with the evidence, and draft the reply
- **OUT OF SCOPE** — real but not this story's problem; name the owning ticket or the person
- **DEFER** — real, in scope, but blocked on a decision; name who decides

**2. Fix only the VALID ones.** Same rules as build mode — the Implementer touches only what the
finding names, never stages, never commits.

**3. Re-run the cheap four**, plus the visual checkpoint if the fix changes rendered output.

**4. Commit the fixes here**, same rule as build mode — the skill commits, never an agent. Reference
the review thread each commit answers.

**5. Hand back to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`** with: what was fixed and in which commit, what was
declined and why, and the evidence behind each decline. **PostBuild owns the push and the
in-thread replies** — every finding gets a written answer, including the declined ones.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never push. Never open or update a PR.** That boundary belongs to PostBuild, which presents
  first and pushes only once Marcel has given the go.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never touch a Tier 1 file** without Marcel naming it and confirming owner approval.
- **Never expand scope.** Something worth doing that the plan didn't ask for gets reported, not
  done. Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Local-only docs are never citable** in a commit message or a code comment. Cite `AGENTS.md`
  or `.claude/rules/*` instead.
- **Say what you could not verify.** Silence reads as "nothing wrong" when it may mean
  "didn't look there".

### Step 2 — `ZimmColourSwatch` atom

Scaffold with `/new-component`; mirror `ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductStyleCode/`.

**Non-obvious sequencing constraint.** Recipe, component and registration land in **one commit**.
`recipeParts.test.ts` walks `overrides/app/components/**` for `*.css.ts` and asserts a sibling
`index.tsx` exists for any recipe declaring `parts:`. A commit with an orphan `.css.ts` **fails
`npm run test`**. Author in order: recipe → registration → component.

**Required Figma read first** — `40000307:13826` (Unselected), `40000307:13831` (Selected),
`40002689:3839` (Focus). Record border width, border colour, outline/offset, inner inset. Map each:

| Value | Token |
|---|---|
| 48px width | `var(--zimm-scale-1200)` — exists |
| 72px height | **no token exists** (gap between `1600`=64 and `3500`=140). Do not add one — Tier 1. Express as `aspectRatio: '2 / 3'` on the 48px width: yields exactly 72px, no raw unit, passes `audit:tokens`. |
| border width | `var(--zimm-border-width-default)` |
| border / selected | `var(--zimm-color-border-default)` / `-secondary` / `-focus` |
| focus ring | `var(--zimm-focus-ring)` + `var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)` |

**Any Figma value with no matching token: STOP and ask.** No invented hex, no `foundation/` edit.

**Recipe** — export `ZimmColourSwatch`; `parts: ['swatch','image']` (selected indicator on the
outer box so it doesn't scale or clip the image); `baseStyle` may be a function of `{selected}` —
safe, because `recipeGuards.test.ts:248-261` always invokes it with an object and walks both
branches. All colour/space as `var(--zimm-*)`.

**Component** — props `{name, imageUrl, href?, isSelected, isFocusable}`.
`useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmColourSwatch', {selected: isSelected})` above any early return.
`const ColourSwatchLink = chakra(RouteLink)` using `Link` from `react-router-dom` — the same import
base `swatch.jsx:16` uses. **This is what delivers AC 4**: a router Link pushes history without a
document load. No `overrides/.../link` component exists.
Render `role="radio"`, `aria-checked`, `aria-label={name}`, `tabIndex={isFocusable ? 0 : -1}`.
The dynamic image URL cannot live in the recipe, so it goes on the element as
`__css={{...styles.image, backgroundImage: `url(${imageUrl})`}}` — the one legitimate dynamic
spread, exactly the shape `footer/footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44,62` already uses.
Falls back to a non-link `chakra.span` when `href` is absent.
**Deliberate divergence from base line 797:** no `backgroundColor={name.toLowerCase()}`. Comment
the reason — (a) it's a CSS keyword coincidence, not a token ("Ivory" resolves, "Bay Blue" doesn't),
unauditable and against `css.md`; (b) it exists to tint behind a *missing* image and AC 5 guarantees
this component never renders without one; (c) `background-size: cover` hides it anyway. Base keeps
it; size still routes through the untouched path.

**Story** — `Commerce/ZimmColourSwatch`; `Default`, `Selected`, `WithoutLink`. **Must add a local
`MemoryRouter` decorator** — `.storybook/preview.tsx` supplies Chakra and Intl only, no router, and
`.storybook/` is Tier 1 so no global decorator is available.

**Test** — wrap in `MemoryRouter`. Assert only this atom's contract: href present → anchor with
that href; href absent → no anchor, still `role="radio"`; `aria-checked` both ways; `tabIndex` 0
vs -1; the resolved URL appears in `background-image`; and a **regression guard** that rendering
with `name="Bay Blue"` leaves `element.style.backgroundColor === ''`.

**Pass criteria** — `tsc`/`lint`/`test`/`audit:tokens` clean, count == baseline ·
`recipeParts.test.ts` output shows a `zimmColourSwatch` case (proves collected, not skipped) ·
`grep -c "ZimmColourSwatch" overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` → 2 ·
raw-value grep on the `.css.ts` returns nothing · no `sx=` in `index.tsx` ·
**mutation check:** flip `aria-checked` to a constant `true`, confirm the selected-state test
fails, revert. A criterion never made to fail does not count.

Both real values now confirmed, and one thing was worth double-checking before I finalize it — the focus ring's Figma export shows asymmetric per-side offsets (`-2px / -2.13px / -3px / -2px`), which looked like it might be a genuine design decision needing your call. Two real corrections to what I'd written in the plan from metadata alone, worth being upfront about:

- **The border-colour mapping was wrong.** The plan guessed `border.default` / `.secondary` / `.focus` across the three states. Direct Figma data shows Unselected has **no border at all**, and both Selected and Focus use the exact same colour — `#191919`, which is `grey[900]`, which only `border.focus` resolves to. `border.default` (light grey) and `.secondary` never come up in this component.
- **Selected's indicator is bottom-only, not a full outline.** The raw export is unambiguous: `border-b`, not `border`. That's a real, deliberate underline-style selected treatment, not something to "correct" to a box border.
