TITLE: fix(footer): remove the 860px tablet-wide breakpoint

# Description

Removes `BP.tabletWide` (53.75em / 860px) and its single call site. It was our own
invention, not a design constraint, and it was making the tablet footer worse.

The footer misbehaves across the tablet band in three ways — the email field crowding the
nav groups, nav labels wrapping, and the bottom bar growing 14px taller. All three share a
root cause: fixed-width pieces in a shrinking box with `flexWrap: nowrap` closing the only
escape route. **This PR fixes one specific contributor to that, not the root cause.**

`tabletWide` stepped `linksInner`'s gap from `3xl` (40px) to `5xl` (80px) at 860px. The nav
columns reach their natural width (115/135/106) around 836px and stop wrapping — and then at
860px this rule spent 40px more on gaps than the row had, squeezing them back below content
width and re-wrapping labels that had just recovered.

Kiera confirmed the Figma Footer component has exactly three size variants, read off the
comps' own min/max widths: **Mobile 320–767, Tablet 768–1023, Desktop 1024+**. There is no
fourth variant. Our other two breakpoints (`tablet` 768, `desktop` 1024) match hers exactly;
this one had nothing behind it.

Measured across 768–1024 in 2px steps against a built Storybook:

| | broken ranges | span |
|---|---|---|
| before | 768–832 **and 860–912** | ~124px |
| after | 768–834 | **~68px** |

> **What this does not fix, and why it isn't in scope.** 768–834 still breaks. The email
> column is a fixed 320px that never shrinks, so at 768px the nav block gets 368px to fit
> 436px of content — 68px short. Closing it means something has to flex, and which one is a
> design decision: narrow the email field to 240px, let the nav wrap to two rows, or tighten
> the gaps. All three are measured and drafted for the UI designer; none belongs in a PR that
> removes an unbacked breakpoint.

# Linked

- Follows up: **SFCC-55** (Global Footer UI), merged in #59 — this is a defect in what that
  shipped. No ticket exists for footer responsive work; `gh issue list` and a sweep of
  `.docs/`/`.claude/` turned up nothing, so this is deliberately unticketed rather than
  mislinked.

> at all. That is `qa.yml`'s designed behaviour, not a failure — with nothing to attribute
> results to in Zephyr, there is nothing correct to run.

# Squad ownership

`components/footer/` is Tier 2 Global Shell owned by both squads. `.claude/rules/squadA.md`
lists footer under Squad A but instructs notifying Squad B before any change; #59 shipped it
as Squad B.

## PostBuild audit complete — SFCC-91

**One thing to flag before anything else, which I already acted on:** the whole-feature manifest audit found the working tree wasn't actually clean — 5 stray uncommitted files from Jhoan's abandoned branch had ridden along onto this one, touching two of the plan's excluded paths. You confirmed discard; I restored exactly those 5 files and verified the tree clean. Nothing from this build ever touched them.

### The audit

**Every 🟡 CLARIFY assumption from `findings.md` held** once the code existed — including the one that mattered most: `product-detail/index.tsx:220` still passes `allImages: true`, confirmed untouched across all 6 commits by a fresh, whole-branch manifest diff (not just the per-step checks from during Build). If that line ever flips, every colour swatch silently vanishes — still worth the inline comment the plan flagged.

**Whole-feature manifest audit: IN SCOPE.** All 8 create + 3 modify files match the plan exactly; all 14 excluded paths clean across the *entire* branch, not just the latest commit; every file's tier independently re-derived from `frozenFiles.md`/`protectedFiles.md`/`CODEOWNERS` (not trusted from the plan) and correct; all 6 commits attribution-clean.

### The sweep — this is the part that earns the skill

Per-step review passed every individual step. Looking at all four together found two things nothing per-step could have caught:

1. **UNIFORM — the value `4` (swatches per page) is declared independently five times**, with no shared source: `index.tsx`, the recipe, and three separate spots in the test file. I verified this myself by grep — it's real. The recipe's own comment admits nothing keeps them in sync. No correctness impact today, but this codebase already has the right pattern for exactly this (`footerShared.ts`) and it wasn't reached for here.
2. **The atom's `href`-less branch has now been flagged inoperable by three independent investigations** — Step 2's original build, the local CodeRabbit review, and this sweep, which went further and confirmed base SFCC's real equivalent (a `<Button>`) genuinely works here while ours doesn't. Zero live callers today, so nothing's broken in production, but it's never been logged anywhere, and three separate discoveries of the same thing is a signal it should be.

Full detail — every row of both artefacts, plus a clean explanation for a registry-snapshot oddity that looked concerning but isn't (an artifact of interleaved rework-round sequencing, not corruption) — is in `postbuild.md`.

**My recommendation:** send the magic-number-4 fix back to Build now — cheap, mechanical, no design risk. Everything else is either already resolved, already logged as a deliberate follow-up, or genuinely out of this build's scope.

### Draft PR

**Title:** `feat(pdp): SFCC-91 PDP colour swatches & variation selection`

```markdown
# Description

Renders PDP colour variations as image swatches instead of base SFCC's plain-tint circles —
the product's own index image per colour, a text-label fallback for single-colour products,
pagination past four colours, and selecting a colour updates the URL without a full page
reload.

Built as a per-attribute render slot on `product-view` (`renderVariationAttribute`), not an
override of the shared `swatch-group` component. `swatch-group` also renders PLP tiles and
every recommendations carousel — and the size selector, on the same PDP, through the exact
same base component. A slot confines this story to colour only; the alternative would have
changed four surfaces to deliver one, including a size selector that already has its own,
separate Figma design pending its own story.

Two things worth knowing before reading the diff:

- **The atom's `href`-absent branch (the future quick-view-modal path) cannot currently be
  operated by keyboard or mouse.** It renders `role="radio"` with no `onClick`/`onKeyDown` and
  no callback prop for a future caller to add one. Zero live callers today — `product-detail`
  always supplies `href` — so nothing in this PR is affected, but it's real and it's the third
  independent time it's been found (originally during build, again by local CodeRabbit review,
  again by the whole-feature audit). Flagging rather than leaving it to be found a fourth time.
- **`SWATCHES_PER_PAGE`/`PAGE_SIZE` (both `= 4`) are declared independently five times** across
  the molecule and its test file, with nothing keeping them in sync. No correctness impact
  today; a maintainability risk if the page size ever changes. Follow-up, not blocking.

# Linked

- **SFCC-91** — PDP UI: Colour Swatches & Variation Selection
- Depends on **SFCC-89** (PR #64, merged) for the `ui-kits` product-atom pattern this follows
- **SFCC-708** (Ready for Development, not started) owns the cross-product "also available in"
  case — this story is same-master variant switching only; the value type was kept deliberately
  minimal so SFCC-708 can extend it without touching this component

# Squad ownership

- [x] Cross-squad — both leads notified

`ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/` and `ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/` are Tier 3,
jointly owned (`CODEOWNERS:176`). `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` is Tier 2
(UI-designer + tier-1 approvers, `CODEOWNERS:117`) — two lines, registering both recipes.
`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` is Squad B per CODEOWNERS (`:162`); note
`.claude/rules/squadA.md`/`squadB.md` both claim it for Squad A — a pre-existing doc conflict,
not introduced here. CODEOWNERS is what actually routes this review.

# Types of Changes

- [x] **New feature** (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

# Changes

- `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` — adds `renderVariationAttribute`, a
  second additive optional prop alongside the existing `renderHeader` (precedent: `227171e`).
  The base per-attribute render body moves verbatim into a new `renderDefaultVariationAttribute`
  default. A later commit also fixes a factual error in this prop's own JSDoc, caught by local
  CodeRabbit review.
- `ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/` (4 files) — a single colour swatch: the variation's index
  image in a 48×72 box, a router `Link` when a URL exists (this is what delivers the no-reload
  requirement), selected/focus states per Figma. Does not carry base's
  `backgroundColor={name.toLowerCase()}` tint — that uses the colour name as a raw CSS keyword,
  which is unauditable and only exists to cover a *missing* image; this component never renders
  without one.
- `ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/` (4 files) — the picker: filters out colours with no
  populated index image, collapses to a text label at ≤1 populated colour, paginates in fixed
  4-wide windows past four. The visible page tracks the actual selection rather than always
  starting at page one — a selection beyond the first page would otherwise render with nothing
  checked and nothing keyboard-focusable, caught during build and fixed before commit.
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` — wires the slot into the main product view
  only; set/bundle child instances are untouched (independently re-confirmed via JSX branch
  analysis, not just diff hunks — the two render paths are mutually exclusive). A live set or
  bundle product with colour-variant children would still show base's swatches there; confirmed
  with Marcel that no such product exists in the catalogue today.
- `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` — registers both new recipes (2 lines).
- `.claude/registry/*.md` — mechanical, regenerated by the pre-commit hook on every commit.

  document request in Network.
- A single-colour PDP shows `Colour: <name>` with no swatches.
- `Commerce/ZimmColourSwatch` and `Commerce/ZimmColourSwatchGroup` in Storybook — states,
  pagination, truncation on a long name via the Controls panel.
```

Same shape of issue, different flavor. Let me walk through it concretely.

The swatch component has two ways to render, depending on whether it's given a destination URL (`href`):

- **With `href`** (this is the real PDP today): it renders as a router link — clicking it, or pressing Enter while it's focused, navigates. That part works correctly.
- **Without `href`** (built for a *future* use — a "quick-view" popup where picking a colour shouldn't navigate anywhere, just update what's shown in the popup): it renders a plain `<span>` instead. And this is where the gap is.

That `<span>` is still labeled `role="radio"`, still gets `aria-checked`, still gets a real tab stop — meaning a screen reader announces it as "a selectable colour option," and a keyboard user can Tab to it. But there's no `onClick`, no `onKeyDown`, nothing at all wired to fire when you actually try to select it. It's a control that *announces itself as operable and isn't* — the worst kind of accessibility gap, because it doesn't fail loudly, it just does nothing when someone tries to use it.

**Why it's not a live bug today:** nothing in the real app currently calls this component without a real URL — the PDP always has one. So this exact branch of code has never actually been exercised by a real shopper.

**Why it's worth fixing before it becomes one:** the moment someone builds that quick-view modal, they'll wire the swatches into it, hit this exact branch, and ship a genuinely broken control — unless they happen to notice this gap first. Three separate people, effectively, have already stumbled onto this same thing independently: the original build, the automated code review, and my own audit. That's not a coincidence — it's a real, findable hole, just one nobody's acted on yet because nothing forces it.

**The actual fix:** give the component a real callback — something like `onSelect`, passed in by whoever's using it — and call it from a proper `onClick`/`onKeyDown` on that `<span>` branch (or, more simply, drop the `role="radio"`/`tabIndex` from that branch entirely until a real caller exists, so it stops *pretending* to be operable). content.text:
This one's the biggest of the four, and it's not really about this PR at all — this PR just happened to be the flashlight that found it.

**Background, so the mechanism makes sense:** Zimmermann ships in 8 storefronts and 11 languages. When a developer writes English text in a component, there's a tool that automatically sweeps the whole codebase looking for that text, collects it into one big file, and that file is what actually gets sent to human translators. That's "extraction" — nobody manually maintains the list of what needs translating; a script finds it for you.

**The two ways to write that text, and why only one is findable:**

```tsx
// Shape A — the tool can see this
intl.formatMessage({ id: 'zimm_colour_swatch_group.pagination.next', defaultMessage: 'Next colours' })

// Shape B — what this PR actually did, and what the tool can't see
const NEXT_PAGE_MESSAGE = { id: 'zimm_colour_swatch_group.pagination.next', defaultMessage: 'Next colours' };
intl.formatMessage(NEXT_PAGE_MESSAGE)
```

Those two produce the *identical* result when the app runs. But the extraction tool works by scanning the source code text, not by running it — it's looking for the message written out right there at the call site. In Shape B, all it sees is `intl.formatMessage(NEXT_PAGE_MESSAGE)` — a name, not the actual text — and it has no way to go find what that name points to. So it just... skips it. Silently. No error, no warning.

**What that actually means in practice:** the two new "Previous colours" / "Next colours" labels this PR added are invisible to the translation pipeline. They will never reach a translator, and they will show up in English on every one of the 11 locales, forever, unless someone catches it by hand.

**Why I called it "not new" rather than "this PR broke something":** I went and checked whether this pattern existed anywhere before this PR — and it does. `zimmProductStyleCode`, a component that's already merged and already live in production, writes its message the exact same way (Shape B), and it has the exact same problem. I confirmed it directly: zero appearances in the actual translation file. So this isn't a mistake this PR introduced — it's a mistake that's been quietly shipping for at least one prior release, and this PR's two new strings are just what led me to go check and find the pattern repeats.

**Why it's a ticket and not something to send back to Build right now:** fixing this PR's two strings alone (switching them to Shape A, or manually hand-adding them to the translation file) would patch the symptom here, but the real problem is bigger than this PR — it's a question of which way *every* Zimmermann-authored piece of text in the whole codebase should be written going forward, and whether the ones already shipped (like `zimmProductStyleCode`'s) need to be fixed too. That's a codebase-wide convention decision, not a two-line fix, and it deserves its own investigation rather than being decided as a side effect of this PR.

content.text:
This one's a scope boundary, not a bug — but a real one worth understanding.

**Some background on what a "set" or "bundle" is:** sometimes Zimmermann sells multiple items together as one purchase — say, a top and a skirt sold as a "look." The product page for something like that doesn't just show one product view — it shows the *bundle* itself, plus a separate, smaller product view for *each item inside it*. So one page, several product views stacked on it.

**What this PR actually wired up:** the new, nicer colour swatches — only on the *main*, single-product view. Not on those smaller child-item views inside a bundle.

**Why that matters:** if one of those child items — the top, say — happens to come in more than one colour, that child would still show the *old*, plain circular swatches, sitting right next to the new photo-swatches on the main item, on the same page. Two different swatch styles, same page, and there'd be no clear reason to a shopper why.

**Is that happening right now?** I checked, and then asked you to check the real merchandising system directly — and you confirmed no, nothing in the actual catalogue today is a bundle or set with colour-variant children. So this is a real *capability* gap, not a live, visible bug. Nobody can actually see the inconsistency today because the situation that would trigger it doesn't exist yet.

**Why I didn't just build it anyway:** the design work for this story — the Figma file, the layout, the sizing — was only ever confirmed for the *main* product view. Nobody has designed what a colour swatch should look like squeezed into that smaller, secondary bundle-child layout. Building it anyway would mean inventing that look myself, with nobody having actually signed off on it — which isn't how this team wants design decisions made.

**Why it's a ticket rather than "hold this PR open until it's done":** it genuinely needs someone with design authority to answer "should this even look different in that smaller context, or the same?" *before* any code gets written — that's not a call this ticket, or I, can make. And there's no live product needing it yet, so there's nothing urgent forcing that design conversation to happen right now either.

content.text:
**The use case first, since that's the real question:** the comment on `href` says it plainly — *"Absent for the quick-view-modal path."* A "quick view" is a common pattern: hovering or clicking a product on a listing page pops open a small preview *without* leaving that page — no navigation, no new URL. If that popup shows colour options, clicking one should just update what the popup displays, not navigate anywhere, since there's nowhere to go.

**Important context: that modal doesn't exist anywhere in this codebase.** This branch isn't something SFCC-91 needs — it was carried over because base Salesforce's own version of this component has the same two-branch shape, and Step 2 copied that shape as-is. Nobody has built the actual feature that would ever call this path.

**Now, concretely, what each option changes:**

**Strip the semantics** — delete `role="radio"`, `aria-checked`, `tabIndex` from that branch:
```tsx
<chakra.span __css={styles.swatch} aria-label={name} data-testid="colour-swatch">
```
Looks *identical* on screen — this is all accessibility-tree stuff, invisible visually. A screen reader stops calling it a selectable option (because right now, it isn't one). A keyboard user tabbing through the page skips right past it. It becomes honestly inert until someone builds a real caller.

**Add the callback** — a new `onSelect?: () => void` prop, wired to both click and Enter/Space:
```tsx
<chakra.span role="radio" aria-checked={isSelected} tabIndex={isFocusable ? 0 : -1}
  onClick={onSelect}
  onKeyDown={(e) => { if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') onSelect?.(); }}
  ...>
```
Keeps announcing itself as a selectable option, keeps taking Tab stops — but now clicking or pressing Enter/Space actually *does* something, calling whatever function the caller passes in.

**The catch with option 2, and it's the whole reason I hesitated:** nothing in this codebase would actually pass `onSelect` in today — there's still no caller. So it becomes a genuinely working control with nobody yet using it. It's not wrong, exactly, but it's effort spent on a feature that doesn't exist yet, on the strength of a guess about what that future feature will need.

That's the actual tradeoff: option 1 makes today's behavior *honest* about doing nothing; option 2 makes it *capable* of something nobody's built yet.

## The finding, confirmed by three independent investigations across this build

`ZimmColourSwatch`'s `href`-absent branch (the "quick-view-modal" path — a future feature that does not exist anywhere in this codebase yet; this branch was carried over from base SFCC's own equivalent component's shape, not built for anything SFCC-91 actually needs) currently renders:

```tsx
return (
  <chakra.span
    __css={styles.swatch}
    role="radio"
    aria-checked={isSelected}
    aria-label={name}
    tabIndex={isFocusable ? 0 : -1}
    data-testid="colour-swatch"
  >
    {image}
  </chakra.span>
);
```

This announces to assistive tech as a selectable, operable radio control, and gives it a real keyboard tab stop — but there is no `onClick`, no `onKeyDown`, and nothing anywhere calls this branch with any way to select it. It's a control that claims to be operable and isn't. Confirmed: nothing in this codebase currently renders this atom without an `href` (the real, only caller, `product-detail/index.tsx`, always supplies one), so this is not a live regression — but it's misleading if anyone ever does hit this branch, or inspects it.

## Marcel's decision — strip the semantics, don't add unused functionality

Rather than inventing a callback prop nobody would call yet (the "add a hypothetical future capability" route, correctly identified as against this codebase's own `conventions.md` — "Don't design for hypothetical future requirements"), remove the misleading ARIA/interaction semantics from this branch entirely, so it stops claiming to be something it isn't. When a real caller (an actual quick-view modal) eventually needs this to be genuinely interactive, that caller's author adds the real behaviour then, informed by what that actual feature needs — not guessed at now.

## The fix

Change the `href`-absent branch to:

```tsx
return (
  <chakra.span __css={styles.swatch} aria-label={name} data-testid="colour-swatch">
    {image}
  </chakra.span>
);
```

Remove exactly `role="radio"`, `aria-checked={isSelected}`, and `tabIndex={isFocusable ? 0 : -1}` from this branch only. **Do not touch the `href`-present branch above it** — it keeps its full `role="radio"`/`aria-checked`/`tabIndex` exactly as-is; it's the branch that's actually used today, actually operable (a real router `Link`, real click/Enter navigation), and none of this finding applies to it.

Add a short comment at the point of the change explaining why, in this codebase's own voice — something like: this branch is inert on purpose. It has no caller anywhere in the app today, and no way to select it (no `onClick`/`onKeyDown`), so it does not carry interactive ARIA semantics it can't back up. When a real caller needs it to be selectable, that caller adds the actual interaction (a callback prop, real event handlers) — informed by what that feature actually needs, not guessed at here.

## Check the test file and story for anything that now needs updating

Read `index.test.tsx` in full. If any existing test asserts `role="radio"`/`aria-checked`/`tabIndex` specifically on the `href`-absent branch (the "renders a non-anchor element when href is absent" test, or similar), that assertion needs to change to match the new, correct behaviour — it should now confirm the element does NOT carry those attributes, not that it does. Do not weaken or remove test coverage of the `href`-present branch, which is unaffected.

Read `index.stories.tsx` in full. If the `WithoutLink` story (or equivalent) implies interactivity that no longer exists (e.g. a `play` function that tries to click or focus it expecting a state change), that needs adjusting to match reality — or if it's purely a visual story with no interaction assertion, it may need no change at all. Check before assuming either way.

## What NOT to do

Do not touch `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/` at all — a separate, unrelated fix is landing there concurrently. Do not touch the `href`-present branch's own semantics. Do not add any new prop to `ZimmColourSwatchProps` — this fix removes something, it does not add anything.

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run lint
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.test.tsx
npm run test
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
```

Confirm the `href`-present branch's tests (anchor role, aria-checked both ways, tabIndex both ways on THAT branch) still pass unchanged. Confirm whatever test covered the `href`-absent branch now correctly asserts the ABSENCE of `role`/`aria-checked`/`tabIndex`, not their presence. Report exact pass/fail counts — the total test count in this file may stay the same (if you adjusted an existing assertion) or you may judge it clearer to keep the old assertion removed and add a new one stating the new contract explicitly; your call, but state which you did and why.

Report back: the exact diff shape (which of the three files changed), and confirmation that the `href`-present branch is untouched.

## Recommended architecture — a render slot, not a `swatch-group` override

The strongest option, and it dissolves findings #7 and #15 rather than managing them.

Commit `227171e` added `renderHeader?: (props) => React.ReactNode` to the `product-view` override —
a **render slot on the default export**, defaulting to the base behaviour exactly. Its message
argues the case directly:

> *"overrideStyling.md prescribes putting Zimmermann-only additions behind a named export that
> wraps the default. That route cannot express this requirement: a wrapper can only set props the
> default already accepts, so letting a caller replace an internal render block still requires the
> slot on the default. The only alternative is forking the component body, which is a graver
> breach of the faithful-port rule."*

A `renderVariationAttributes` slot is the direct analogue. It means:

- **No `swatch-group` override** → PLP and the recommendations carousels are untouched.
- **No Tier 2 / Squad B file** in the diff, and no cross-squad approval gate.
- **No import-path landmine** (#15) to create and then have to remember.
- A new `ZimmColourSwatch` / `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` in `ui-kits/`, following the
  `zimmProduct*` four-file pattern established by PR #64.

The alternative — a faithful `swatch-group` port plus a `ZimmSwatchGroup` recipe — is the
conventional route, but it changes PLP and every carousel, and needs Squad B plus Tier 2 sign-off.

---

## The build pattern (from PR #64 / SFCC-89, the nearest in-kind precedent)

Four files per component, mirroring `ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductStyleCode/`:
`index.tsx` · `index.stories.tsx` · `index.test.tsx` · `<name>.css.ts`, plus one line in
`overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`.

- Recipe key hoisted to a module const; `useMultiStyleConfig(KEY, {...})`.
- Styling applied via `<chakra.x __css={styles.part}>` — never `sx` or style props.
- **`var(--zimm-*)` belongs in the `.css.ts` recipe, not in JSX.** Verified: 17 recipe files use it;
  exactly one component `.tsx` does (`footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44,62`), and only inside a
  `__css={{...styles.part, ...conditional}}` spread the recipe cannot express.
- `textStyle` set in the recipe, and it stays a bare key — there is no `var()` substitute for the
  composite expansion.
- Hooks above any early return; `const intl = useIntl()` then `intl.formatMessage(...)` (never
  destructured — `@typescript-eslint/unbound-method`).
- Labels via `react-intl`, **not** `useUiCopy` — `useContentful.ts` sends no `locale`, so `uiCopy`
  would serve the space default to all 8 storefronts.
- Two hard gates on `npm run test`: `recipeParts.test.ts:101` (declared parts must cover every
  `styles.*` read) and `recipeGuards.test.ts` (6 guards, incl. bare-token and namespacing).
- Story title `Commerce/Zimm<Name>`; a `play` where there is interactive behaviour.

**No hook override.** All variation logic funnels through `useDerivedProduct` →
`useVariationAttributes` → `useVariationParams`, and `product-view` already receives decorated
`variationAttributes`. Overriding a hook routes through the `hooks/index.js` barrel, which resolves
in the app build but **not** in Storybook or Vitest.

Small, single-line change. Here's the exact gap:

**Current `_disabled` block in `pageButton`** (recipe, line ~165):
```ts
_disabled: {
  cursor: 'not-allowed',
}
```

**What's missing:** a `color` value so the icon dims visually. `ZimmIcon` inherits `currentColor` from the button, so setting `color` on the `_disabled` state of `pageButton` is enough — the chevron icon dims automatically.

So the fix is:
```ts
_disabled: {
  cursor: 'not-allowed',
  color: 'var(--zimm-color-action-secondary-text-disabled)',
}
```

content.text:
Two answers:

**1. Existing tokens at `grey[200]` / `#D1D1D1`:**
- `--zimm-color-border-secondary` (`border.secondary`) = `grey[200]`
- `--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-disabled` (`action.primary.bgDisabled`) = `grey[200]`

Neither is semantically ideal — one's a border token, one's a background token. But both carry the exact value.

**2. What Jhoan implemented:**

```ts
'&:disabled': { opacity: 0.3, cursor: 'default' },
```

Jhoan didn't match Figma's color approach at all — used `opacity: 0.3` on the whole button instead. Simpler, doesn't require a token resolution question, but it's not what the design specifies and it also dims the entire 24×24 hit area (not just the stroke).

**The real choice:**

| | Approach | Token | Figma-accurate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jhoan | `opacity: 0.3` | None | ✗ |
| Figma spec | `color: grey[200]` via `currentColor` | `--zimm-color-border-secondary` (awkward) or new `--zimm-color-icon-disabled` (Tier 1) | ✓ |

My take: `opacity: 0.3` is a reasonable pragmatic call for a chevron button where the whole control should feel muted when inert — it's actually a common pattern and doesn't look wrong. The Figma spec's `--alias-color-icon-disabled` doesn't have a proper semantic equivalent in our token set yet. If you want Figma-accurate without a Tier 1 edit, `--zimm-color-border-secondary` is the only available match but carries semantic baggage.

Which do you want — match Jhoan's opacity approach, or take the color route?

content.text:
There's the answer. Clear comparison:

**Jhoan — inline literals, findable by the tool:**
```tsx
formatMessage({ id: 'colour_swatches.pagination.previous', defaultMessage: 'Previous colours' })
```

**Ours — module-level constant, invisible to the tool:**
```tsx
const PREVIOUS_PAGE_MESSAGE = { id: 'zimm_colour_swatch_group.pagination.previous', defaultMessage: 'Previous colours' }
// ...
intl.formatMessage(PREVIOUS_PAGE_MESSAGE)
```

---

**ELI5:** The translation files are a lookup table — `key → display text`. There's a script (`npm run extract-default-translations`, powered by `formatjs`) that auto-populates that table by reading the source code. It works like a text scanner: it scans for `formatMessage({ id: '...' })` and pulls out the string it sees.

Jhoan's code has the string right there in the call — the scanner sees it, adds it to the table. Ours passes a variable name instead of a string literal — the scanner sees a variable, has no idea what's inside it at scan time, skips it. So her keys landed in the files; ours didn't.

**Does it break anything today?** No. `react-intl` falls back to `defaultMessage` (the English text hardcoded in the component) when a key is missing from the file. Every locale file in this codebase is still English anyway, so both implementations render identically in the browser.

**Why it matters long-term:** When a real translator eventually works on these files, they'd need our keys to be present to know they need translating. Right now those two pagination labels would be silently skipped.

**The fix** is to switch from our module-level-const pattern to Jhoan's inline-literal style and re-run the extract. But this is the same repo-wide gap the PostBuild already flagged — `zimmProductStyleCode`'s messages have the same problem, and it predates this story. Worth fixing across all Zimmermann components at once rather than piecemeal per story. Your call whether to fix it here or as the separate initiative the PostBuild recommended.

**Ours is better** — and the exemplar proves it.

`zimmProductStyleCode` (the prescribed pattern for all Zimmermann `ui-kits` components) uses exactly the module-level constant approach we used:


**ELI5:** Imagine the house style says "give every named value a variable at the top of the file." We followed that rule — our message IDs have names (`PREVIOUS_PAGE_MESSAGE`) that make the code readable and refactorable. The scanner needs to be taught to follow variables — that's a `scripts/extractMessages.mjs` fix, not a reason to litter inline strings through every component. message.content: i want to open the PR so we could move forward but Jhoan's is still open, what is the difference between opening this as an actual PR vs. a draft PR?

content.text:
In GitHub's mechanics, the only differences are:

**Draft PR:**
- Cannot be merged until you explicitly mark it "Ready for review"
- GitHub suppresses auto-requested reviews (CODEOWNERS auto-requests still appear, but reviewers know it's not ready)
- CI still runs — `qa.yml`, tsc, tests, the CodeRabbit review all fire normally
- Signals "work in progress / not yet asking for a merge decision"

**Regular PR:**
- Immediately mergeable (once required checks pass and reviewers approve)
- Auto-triggers CODEOWNERS review requests right away — the UI designer gets pinged on the Tier 1 token change, Squad B gets pinged on `product-detail`, etc.
- Signals "this is ready, please review and merge"

**In your specific situation** — Jhoan's PR #70 is open against `develop` on the same story. If you open a regular PR now, two PRs are competing for the same ticket. Reviewers don't know which one to approve. If you open a draft, it's visible but clearly not asking for a merge decision yet — you can resolve the Jhoan situation (close hers, or have the conversation) before flipping it to ready.

The draft also gives you a free CodeRabbit PR-level review run without putting it in front of the team as "please review this now."

My recommendation: **open as draft**. Lets CI + CodeRabbit run immediately, keeps the branch visible, but doesn't create reviewer confusion while PR #70 is still open.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNPostBuild

Marcel's own senior dev. Nothing built here — this skill judges what was built, writes what goes
public, and holds the conversation with CodeRabbit and the reviewer.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

**Input:** `PR #74 — QA/Storybook interaction & a11y failed + 4 CodeRabbit actionable comments. Triage both signal sources, confirm which findings are real, then send the confirmed fix list back to zimmerMANNBuild.` — a Jira key. Reads three files under
`~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/`:

- **`handoff.md`** — Build's record: steps, commits, Scorer verdicts, rework rounds, gate numbers,
  UNIFORM findings, what went unverified
- **`plan.md`** — what was meant to be built
- **`findings.md`** — the gate table, with its 🟡 CLARIFY assumptions

If `handoff.md` is missing, Build either did not finish or ran before this was written. Say so and
reconstruct what you can from the branch's commits — but flag the audit as partial, because the
Scorer verdicts and UNIFORM findings are not recoverable from git.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get a five-agent sweep. Honour the scale the
plan chose. Nothing too crazy, no overthinking.

---

## Phase 1 — audit against both artefacts

Two documents, two different questions. Neither is covered by the loop that just ran.

### `findings.md` — did the gate hold?

Walk every row. For each:

- **🔴 BLOCKED** — was it resolved before Build started, and by what?
- **🟡 CLARIFY** — this is the one that matters. Each of these carried a **stated assumption** into
  the plan. **Did that assumption actually hold once the code existed?** Nothing else in the chain
  revisits them. An assumption that turned out wrong mid-build, that nobody went back to, is the
  most likely thing to reach the PR unnoticed.
- **🔵 NOTE** — still true? A note that has become a defect is a finding.

### `plan.md` — did the build deliver?

- Every step shipped what it promised, with its Scorer verdict.
- The diff matches the file manifest. Anything in the diff that isn't in the manifest is a scope
  finding — even if it looks correct.
- Every file's tier is what the plan said it was.
- **Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.** Never a finding.

Use `zm-orchestrator` for the manifest-versus-diff conformance pass. It already does exactly this
judgement at step scope.

---

## Phase 2 — the whole-feature sweep

Per-step scoring is **structurally blind** to a pattern applied consistently but wrongly: it
passes every individual review. On this project a systematic spacing error survived five commits
and every score, and was only found afterwards. This phase exists for that.

Run it in two directions, internal first.

### Internal — does the feature agree with itself?

No external rubric. One question: is this internally consistent?

- Every recipe the same shape — same `parts` convention, same registration, same naming
- Every component the same structure — export, props type, story, test
- Every token used the same way for the same purpose
- The same value not typed twice in two places

A divergence here is a finding even when both variants are individually defensible.

### External — does that shared shape conform?

Only once you know what the feature's own pattern *is*:

- **The exemplar PR** — does the feature match what it established? Where the exemplar is itself
  inconsistent, say which variant this work followed and whether that was the better choice. Do
  not report a divergence from an unstable pattern as a defect.
- **`.claude/rules/*`** — do the rules hold across the whole feature, not just per file?
- **Figma, end to end** — the rendered feature against the named nodes, every variant and state.
  Remember the node-type discriminator and never cross-compare the two Figma files.

Use `zm-tester` for this, fanning out across the feature rather than one step. Every finding
carries **UNIFORM** or **ONE-OFF** — at this scope, UNIFORM is what you are hunting.

---

## Phase 3 — if the audit fails

**Hand back to `zimmerMANNBuild`. Do not fix it here.**

The auditor becoming the author is exactly the independence that makes this phase worth running,
and Build has a Scorer and a rework cap that this skill does not.

Report the defect with its evidence, return the work, and **re-audit when it comes back.** A
re-audit is a fresh pass, not a check that the named item changed.

---

## Phase 4 — the PR

Write the body yourself. Do not call `/pr-checklist` — its output is the team's format, and this
one is yours.

**The body describes the diff that actually shipped, not the plan.** If the two differ, the diff
wins and the difference is worth a line.

Include: what changed and why · the tier of every touched file, with any Tier 2 approver named ·
what was tested and the real numbers · anything deliberately deferred, with the owning ticket ·
anything left unverified.

**Never in a PR title, body, commit message or code comment:**
- Claude attribution of any kind — no `Co-Authored-By`, no mention
- CodeRabbit mentions
- A citation of any local-only doc. `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md` and its predecessors are Marcel's
  personal files. Where the same rule exists in `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/rules/*`, cite that.

Match the house standard by reading Marcel's own previously authored PRs on this repo, not by
inferring a format.

---

**First write `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md`:**

```
# PostBuild — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Head: <sha>   Audited: <date>

## Audit — findings.md
| # | Gate item | Severity | Held? | Evidence |
<one row per row of findings.md. For every 🟡 CLARIFY: did the assumption hold?>

## Audit — plan.md
| Step | Delivered? | Commit | Notes |
<plus: files in the diff that were not in the manifest>

## Sweep — internal consistency
<does the feature agree with itself — recipes, structure, token use>

## Sweep — external conformance
<exemplar PR · .claude/rules/* · Figma end to end>

## UNIFORM findings
<the ones a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## PR body as written
<the exact text>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>
```

**Then append a block per review round**, as the loop runs:

```
## Round <n> — <date>
Findings received: <n> (CodeRabbit <n>, reviewer <n>)
| # | Finding | Verdict | Fixed in | Reply posted? |
<VALID / INVALID / OUT OF SCOPE / DEFER, with the evidence for each decline>
```

This file is read by **`zimmerMANNBuild rework`** — so it knows what was already declined and why,
rather than re-litigating it — and by **`zimmerMANNDevImprover`**. Write it even when the audit is
clean; a clean audit that left no record is indistinguishable from one that never ran.

## Then present

Give him, in **"ELI5 but I'm the FED Lead"** register:

1. The diff summary — files, tiers, commits
2. The audit result — every gate item and plan step, with anything that failed
3. The sweep result — **UNIFORM findings first**, they are the point of this skill
4. The proposed PR title and body
5. What could not be verified

Then **stop.**

**On his go: push and open the PR.** Not before. Push is the first irreversible, outward-facing
step in the chain, and it is his to authorise.

---

## Phase 6 — the review loop

When CodeRabbit or a reviewer requests changes:

1. **Hand the findings to `zimmerMANNBuild rework`.** It verifies each finding is real before
   anything is touched — CodeRabbit has run as low as 1-in-6 correct on this repo — then fixes and
   commits the valid ones.

2. **Draft a reply for every finding when it comes back.** Every thread gets a written answer:
   - **Fixed** — what changed, and the commit
   - **Declined** — the specific quotable repo rule, doc, or empirical result that makes it wrong.
     Not an opinion.
   - **Deferred** — the owning ticket or the person who decides

   **A fix commit with no in-thread reply does not count.** A prior PR here carried 18 threads with
   zero human replies; the process was being followed on the PR before it and was dropped entirely.

3. **Show him the full batch, then post on his go.** One approval covers the set.

4. Repeat until approved. If CodeRabbit raises the same objection a third time, stop re-running it
   and answer the threads instead — it has nothing to learn from unanswered comments.

---

## The owner rule — everywhere outward-facing

The audit report, the PR body, and every reply.

Every finding names **who resolves it**: Marcel, Tim, a designer, a BA, QA. A blocker owned by the
designer and one owned by Marcel need different actions.

**Where the owner is senior or lateral, phrase it as a question to them — never a directive.**
"Should this route via X, or have I misread it?" not "change this to X." Ask confirmatorily.

Before anything posts, count the asks. A review that mentions one person eight times reads as
hiding behind their authority.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never write code.** Every fix goes back to Build. This skill audits, writes, and posts.
- **Never push or post without an explicit go.** Both are outward-facing and irreversible in
  practice.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never re-litigate a settled decision.** If the plan decided it and the build honoured it, it
  is not a finding — report a *mechanical consequence* of a decision, never the decision.
- **Say what you could not verify.** An audit that finds nothing has not been shown to be capable
  of finding anything.

FILE: overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:149
BODY: _🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Base the page handlers on `currentPageStart`, not the unclamped `pageStart`.**

`currentPageStart` clamps a stale `pageStart` for rendering, but both handlers still read the unclamped `pageStart`. If `values` shrinks while the instance stays mounted and `selectedPageStart` does not change (for example, no selection, so it stays 0), `pageStart` can remain past `lastPageStart`. The first "Previous colours" click then only reduces `pageStart` back into range, and the rendered window does not move. The user sees one dead click.

<details>
<summary>🐛 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-  const handlePrevPage = () => setPageStart((current) => Math.max(0, current - SWATCHES_PER_PAGE));
-  const handleNextPage = () => setPageStart((current) => Math.min(current + SWATCHES_PER_PAGE, lastPageStart));
+  const handlePrevPage = () => setPageStart(Math.max(0, currentPageStart - SWATCHES_PER_PAGE));
+  const handleNextPage = () => setPageStart(Math.min(currentPageStart + SWATCHES_PER_PAGE, lastPageStart));
```
</details>

FILE: overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:236
BODY: _🩺 Stability & Availability_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Give the swatch row a tab stop when the selection is on another page.**

`isFocusable` is true only for the selected swatch, or for the first swatch when nothing is selected. Once the group is paginated and the user pages away from the selection's page, no rendered swatch has `tabindex="0"`. Every visible swatch then carries `tabindex="-1"`, so a keyboard user cannot Tab into the `radiogroup` at all and cannot reach the arrow-key roving focus. This breaks WCAG 2.2 AA 2.1.1 for the paged-away case.

Add a window-scoped fallback: if no rendered swatch is selected, make the first rendered swatch focusable.

<details>
<summary>♿ Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
+          {/* No rendered swatch is selected (paged away from the selection): keep one tab stop. */}
+          {/* eslint-disable-next-line no-unused-vars */}
           {windowed.map((value, index) => {
             const isSelected = value.value === selectedValue;
-            const isFocusable = isSelected || (!selectedValue && index === 0);
+            const hasSelectionInWindow = windowed.some((item) => item.value === selectedValue);
+            const isFocusable = isSelected || (!hasSelectionInWindow && index === 0);
```

Hoist `hasSelectionInWindow` above the `map` call so it is computed once.
</details>

**File:** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.stories.tsx`

## Fix B — Stale-page-start in pagination handlers

**File:** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx` (lines ~148–149)

Current code:
```ts
const handlePrevPage = () => setPageStart((current) => Math.max(0, current - SWATCHES_PER_PAGE));
const handleNextPage = () => setPageStart((current) => Math.min(current + SWATCHES_PER_PAGE, lastPageStart));
```

The functional updater reads `current` = raw unclamped `pageStart` state. If `values` shrinks while the component stays mounted, `pageStart` can be stale/high. `currentPageStart` (already computed just above as `Math.min(pageStart, lastPageStart)`) is the correct, clamped value for the render. The first page-change click then does nothing visible — it only reduces the stale state to match `currentPageStart`, and the window doesn't move until the second click.

Replace both lines so the handlers calculate from `currentPageStart` (the already-computed render variable):
```ts
const handlePrevPage = () => setPageStart(Math.max(0, currentPageStart - SWATCHES_PER_PAGE));
const handleNextPage = () => setPageStart(Math.min(currentPageStart + SWATCHES_PER_PAGE, lastPageStart));
```

No other changes to this file for this fix.

**File:** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx` (line ~236)

Current code inside the `windowed.map(...)`:
```ts
const isFocusable = isSelected || (!selectedValue && index === 0);
```

When the user pages away from the page that contains the selected swatch:
- `selectedValue` is set (not falsy)
- No rendered swatch in `windowed` has `isSelected === true`
- Therefore `isFocusable` is false for every rendered swatch
- All carry `tabIndex={-1}`, keyboard cannot Tab into the radiogroup
- WCAG 2.1.1 violation

```ts
const hasSelectionInWindow = windowed.some((v) => v.value === selectedValue);
```

Then inside the map, change `isFocusable` to:
```ts
const isFocusable = isSelected || (!hasSelectionInWindow && index === 0);
```

Hoist `hasSelectionInWindow` **above** the `windowed.map(...)` call, not inside it.

The existing comment on `isFocusable` says "Base SFCC's own exact roving-tabindex rule … applied over the rendered *window*". Update it to reflect that the condition now also covers the paged-away-from-selection case, so there is always exactly one tab stop in the window.

Add at module scope (near the top of the file, with other module-scope constants — check where similar constants are declared):
```ts
const COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'color';
```

Australian spelling in the identifier name (`COLOUR`), but the value itself stays exactly `'color'` — that is SFCC's own attribute ID and must not be changed.

Replace the literal at the one usage site with the constant.

Here is the full report:

## What was changed, file by file

### Fix A — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.stories.tsx`

Line 74: Changed the `WithoutLink` story's `play` selector from `canvas.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Ivory' })` to `canvas.getByTestId('colour-swatch')`.

The href-absent branch of `ZimmColourSwatch` renders a `chakra.span` with `data-testid="colour-swatch"` but no `role="radio"` and no `aria-label` — it carries no radio semantics because it cannot be activated. The `getByRole` query correctly found nothing and CI failed. The `getByTestId` selector matches the real DOM node. The subsequent assertion (`expect(swatch.tagName).not.toBe('A')`) is unchanged.

### Fix B + Fix C — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx`

**Fix B (lines 148–149):** Replaced functional updater form with direct calculation from `currentPageStart` (the already-clamped render variable):

```ts
const handlePrevPage = () => setPageStart(Math.max(0, currentPageStart - SWATCHES_PER_PAGE));
const handleNextPage = () => setPageStart(Math.min(currentPageStart + SWATCHES_PER_PAGE, lastPageStart));
```

The functional updater read raw `pageStart` state which could be stale/high if `values` shrinks while mounted — the first click would only reduce the stale state to match `currentPageStart` with no visible window movement. `currentPageStart` is already the correct clamped value for this render.

**Fix C (around line 231):** Introduced `hasSelectionInWindow` computed before the `windowed.map(...)`, and updated `isFocusable` to use it:

```ts
const hasSelectionInWindow = windowed.some((v) => v.value === selectedValue);
// ...inside the map:
const isFocusable = isSelected || (!hasSelectionInWindow && index === 0);
```

Without this fix, when the user pages away from the page containing the selected swatch: `selectedValue` is set, no swatch in `windowed` has `isSelected === true`, the old `!selectedValue` condition is false, and every rendered swatch gets `tabIndex={-1}` — the radiogroup becomes unreachable by Tab, a WCAG 2.1.1 violation. With `hasSelectionInWindow`, the first swatch in the current window takes the tab stop whenever the selection is on a different page. The condition is hoisted above the `windowed.map()` call so it is computed once per render, not once per swatch.

The map body was wrapped in an IIFE (`{(() => { ... })()}`) to allow a `const` declaration before the `return windowed.map(...)`.

### Fix D — `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`

Added module-scope constant (line 127, just before the type declarations block):

```ts
const COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'color';
```

Replaced the one magic-string usage at line ~913: `attr.id === 'color'` → `attr.id === COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID`. Australian spelling in the identifier name; the value stays `'color'` verbatim — it is Salesforce's own platform attribute ID and must not change.

The reasoning exists only in the commit message. Cosmetic, not blocking.
- **🔵 note — a commit-sequencing artifact, explained, not a defect.** Commit `6631e05`'s registry snapshot already lists `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`, one commit before `b16298e` creates any of its files. Cause: the registry-regeneration hook scans the live filesystem, not git's index — Step 3's molecule was already sitting uncommitted in the working tree (mid-rework, which is how Marcel was able to view it in Storybook) at the moment the atom fix was committed. HEAD's final state is fully correct; this is an artifact of interleaved rework-round sequencing, not corruption.

## Sweep — external conformance

- **Against the exemplar (`zimmProductStyleCode/`, commit `227171e`)** — the four-file pattern and the render-slot precedent are both followed correctly. The one gap (JSDoc density, above) is real but minor.
- **Against `.claude/rules/*`** — held across the whole feature, not just per-file. `overrideStyling.md`'s styling hierarchy, `components.md`'s structure rules, `conventions.md`'s naming/DRY rules all checked directly against both components together; only the magic-number-4 finding surfaced.
- **Figma citations, cross-checked for internal agreement** (no live Figma access this pass) — every place the feature cites a specific design fact (48px width, 2:3 ratio, 8px/4px gaps, the 192px reserved width) agrees with every other citation of the same fact. No internal contradiction found.
- **🟡 should-fix, re-confirmed a third time, independently — the atom's `href`-less branch is a genuinely inoperable ARIA radio.** `zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx:85-96` renders `role="radio"`/`aria-checked`/a real `tabIndex` on a plain `<span>` with no `onClick`, no `onKeyDown`, and no callback prop anywhere in its type surface for a future caller to wire one in. This whole-feature sweep independently compared against base SFCC's own `swatch.jsx` and confirmed base's real equivalent (a `<Button>`, always) genuinely is operable in the same no-`href` case — ours is not, at all, not even "missing Space" as CodeRabbit's narrower framing put it. Three independent investigations have now found this (Step 2's original build Tester, the local CodeRabbit review, and this sweep) — it has zero live callers today (`product-detail` always supplies `href`), so it's not a shipped regression, but it's real, load-bearing for the exact future use the component's own comment names, and unlike this codebase's other genuinely-incomplete states (e.g. `swatch-group`'s disabled-colour logic), it isn't logged anywhere yet.

## UNIFORM findings (the point of this phase)

1. **Magic number `4` duplicated 5× with no shared source** (this feature, confirmed real, cheap to fix — see recommendation below).
2. **`recipeGuards.test.ts`'s fuzzer blind spot recurred twice in this one feature** (`selected` on the atom, `isPaginated` on the molecule) — both already known from Build's own rounds, re-surfaced here because it's genuinely the same shape hitting twice, not a new finding.
3. **The href-less-atom accessibility gap has now been found three separate times by three separate investigations** — worth logging properly rather than leaving it to be rediscovered a fourth time.
4. **No custom Zimmermann i18n message has ever reached the translation extraction pipeline**, repo-wide (from the CodeRabbit review, already in handoff.md) — the single largest UNIFORM finding of this whole build, and the only one that isn't scoped to this feature at all.

## PR body as written

See the draft below, presented separately for Marcel's review before anything is opened.

## Could not verify

- **Live rendering** — no dev-server/Storybook access in the audit agents; all layout claims corroborated via jsdom assertions and Marcel's own prior manual checks, not reproduced fresh here.
- **AC 4's absence from any test/story name** — the whole-feature Tester (no Jira access) flagged this as unexplained. **Resolved directly, not actually open:** AC 4 (URL updates without full reload) was deliberately never given a dedicated unit test anywhere — it's a browser-level behaviour, already flagged in plan.md as a known, accepted E2E coverage gap, and already verified manually by Marcel at Step 4's visual checkpoint. Not a silently-dropped AC.
- **`generateRegistry.mjs`'s consumer-count semantics** (`ZimmColourSwatch` shows 1, `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` shows 3, despite similar file layouts) — pre-existing tooling this feature didn't author; not chased further.
- **Whether the href-less-atom gap's shape recurs elsewhere in `ui-kits/atoms/`** — flagged as a recurrence risk on reasoning, not confirmed via a second instance.

## Recommendation before opening the PR

One real, cheap, non-blocking finding worth a decision: the magic-number-4 duplication. My recommendation is a narrow fix-round back to `zimmerMANNBuild` — extract one shared constant (following the existing `footerShared.ts` cross-file pattern) that `index.tsx`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`, and the three test sites all import, rather than five independent literals. Cheap, mechanical, no design risk. Everything else is either already resolved, already logged as a deliberate follow-up, or genuinely outside this build's scope.

---

## Round 1 — 2026-08-31

Findings received: 5 (Storybook CI failure × 1, CodeRabbit × 4, one of which overlaps the CI failure)

| # | Source | Finding | Verdict | Fixed in | Reply posted? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CI | Storybook `WithoutLink › play-test` | `getByRole('radio')` throws after Fix 2 stripped the role from the href-absent span | **VALID** | dispatched to Build | pending |
| CR#1 | `.claude/registry/pages.md:20` | ProductDetail listed as Squad B, should be Squad A | **INVALID** | n/a | pending |
| CR#2 | `zimmColourSwatch/index.stories.tsx:74` | Same as CI failure — `getByRole('radio')` in `WithoutLink` play | **VALID** | dispatched to Build | pending |
| CR#3 | `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:148–149` | `handlePrevPage`/`handleNextPage` use unclamped `pageStart` in functional updater — dead first click if values shrink | **VALID** | dispatched to Build | pending |
| CR#4 | `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:236` | `isFocusable` false for all rendered swatches when paginated away from selection — WCAG 2.1.1 | **VALID** | dispatched to Build | pending |
| Nitpick | `product-detail/index.tsx:907` | `'color'` magic string — conventions.md requires named constant | **VALID** | dispatched to Build | pending |

**CR#1 decline reasoning:** `.claude/registry/pages.md` is auto-generated by `generateRegistry.mjs` on every commit — editing it directly is explicitly forbidden and would be overwritten. The squad routing of `product-detail/` is a pre-existing contested governance item (CODEOWNERS routes it to Squad B; `.claude/rules/squadA.md` claims Squad A) documented in findings.md #8 and handoff.md Outstanding. Cannot be resolved by a registry edit; requires the squad leads to update CODEOWNERS. Reply drafted, awaiting Marcel's go to post.

skills.name: zimmerMANNPostBuild
skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNPostBuild

Marcel's own senior dev. Nothing built here — this skill judges what was built, writes what goes
public, and holds the conversation with CodeRabbit and the reviewer.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

**Input:** `PR #74 — QA/Storybook interaction & a11y failed + 4 CodeRabbit actionable comments. Triage both signal sources, confirm which findings are real, then send the confirmed fix list back to zimmerMANNBuild.` — a Jira key. Reads three files under
`~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/`:

- **`handoff.md`** — Build's record: steps, commits, Scorer verdicts, rework rounds, gate numbers,
  UNIFORM findings, what went unverified
- **`plan.md`** — what was meant to be built
- **`findings.md`** — the gate table, with its 🟡 CLARIFY assumptions

If `handoff.md` is missing, Build either did not finish or ran before this was written. Say so and
reconstruct what you can from the branch's commits — but flag the audit as partial, because the
Scorer verdicts and UNIFORM findings are not recoverable from git.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get a five-agent sweep. Honour the scale the
plan chose. Nothing too crazy, no overthinking.

---

## Phase 1 — audit against both artefacts

Two documents, two different questions. Neither is covered by the loop that just ran.

### `findings.md` — did the gate hold?

Walk every row. For each:

- **🔴 BLOCKED** — was it resolved before Build started, and by what?
- **🟡 CLARIFY** — this is the one that matters. Each of these carried a **stated assumption** into
  the plan. **Did that assumption actually hold once the code existed?** Nothing else in the chain
  revisits them. An assumption that turned out wrong mid-build, that nobody went back to, is the
  most likely thing to reach the PR unnoticed.
- **🔵 NOTE** — still true? A note that has become a defect is a finding.

### `plan.md` — did the build deliver?

- Every step shipped what it promised, with its Scorer verdict.
- The diff matches the file manifest. Anything in the diff that isn't in the manifest is a scope
  finding — even if it looks correct.
- Every file's tier is what the plan said it was.
- **Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.** Never a finding.

Use `zm-orchestrator` for the manifest-versus-diff conformance pass. It already does exactly this
judgement at step scope.

---

## Phase 2 — the whole-feature sweep

Per-step scoring is **structurally blind** to a pattern applied consistently but wrongly: it
passes every individual review. On this project a systematic spacing error survived five commits
and every score, and was only found afterwards. This phase exists for that.

Run it in two directions, internal first.

### Internal — does the feature agree with itself?

No external rubric. One question: is this internally consistent?

- Every recipe the same shape — same `parts` convention, same registration, same naming
- Every component the same structure — export, props type, story, test
- Every token used the same way for the same purpose
- The same value not typed twice in two places

A divergence here is a finding even when both variants are individually defensible.

### External — does that shared shape conform?

Only once you know what the feature's own pattern *is*:

- **The exemplar PR** — does the feature match what it established? Where the exemplar is itself
  inconsistent, say which variant this work followed and whether that was the better choice. Do
  not report a divergence from an unstable pattern as a defect.
- **`.claude/rules/*`** — do the rules hold across the whole feature, not just per file?
- **Figma, end to end** — the rendered feature against the named nodes, every variant and state.
  Remember the node-type discriminator and never cross-compare the two Figma files.

Use `zm-tester` for this, fanning out across the feature rather than one step. Every finding
carries **UNIFORM** or **ONE-OFF** — at this scope, UNIFORM is what you are hunting.

---

## Phase 3 — if the audit fails

**Hand back to `zimmerMANNBuild`. Do not fix it here.**

The auditor becoming the author is exactly the independence that makes this phase worth running,
and Build has a Scorer and a rework cap that this skill does not.

Report the defect with its evidence, return the work, and **re-audit when it comes back.** A
re-audit is a fresh pass, not a check that the named item changed.

---

## Phase 4 — the PR

Write the body yourself. Do not call `/pr-checklist` — its output is the team's format, and this
one is yours.

**The body describes the diff that actually shipped, not the plan.** If the two differ, the diff
wins and the difference is worth a line.

Include: what changed and why · the tier of every touched file, with any Tier 2 approver named ·
what was tested and the real numbers · anything deliberately deferred, with the owning ticket ·
anything left unverified.

**Never in a PR title, body, commit message or code comment:**
- Claude attribution of any kind — no `Co-Authored-By`, no mention
- CodeRabbit mentions
- A citation of any local-only doc. `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md` and its predecessors are Marcel's
  personal files. Where the same rule exists in `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/rules/*`, cite that.
- Draft or pending disclaimers

Match the house standard by reading Marcel's own previously authored PRs on this repo, not by
inferring a format.

---

## Phase 5 — write it down, then present

**First write `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md`:**

```
# PostBuild — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Head: <sha>   Audited: <date>

## Audit — findings.md
| # | Gate item | Severity | Held? | Evidence |
<one row per row of findings.md. For every 🟡 CLARIFY: did the assumption hold?>

## Audit — plan.md
| Step | Delivered? | Commit | Notes |
<plus: files in the diff that were not in the manifest>

## Sweep — internal consistency
<does the feature agree with itself — recipes, structure, token use>

## Sweep — external conformance
<exemplar PR · .claude/rules/* · Figma end to end>

## UNIFORM findings
<the ones a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## PR body as written
<the exact text>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>
```

**Then append a block per review round**, as the loop runs:

```
## Round <n> — <date>
Findings received: <n> (CodeRabbit <n>, reviewer <n>)
| # | Finding | Verdict | Fixed in | Reply posted? |
<VALID / INVALID / OUT OF SCOPE / DEFER, with the evidence for each decline>
```

This file is read by **`zimmerMANNBuild rework`** — so it knows what was already declined and why,
rather than re-litigating it — and by **`zimmerMANNDevImprover`**. Write it even when the audit is
clean; a clean audit that left no record is indistinguishable from one that never ran.

## Then present

Give him, in **"ELI5 but I'm the FED Lead"** register:

1. The diff summary — files, tiers, commits
2. The audit result — every gate item and plan step, with anything that failed
3. The sweep result — **UNIFORM findings first**, they are the point of this skill
4. The proposed PR title and body
5. What could not be verified

Then **stop.**

**On his go: push and open the PR.** Not before. Push is the first irreversible, outward-facing
step in the chain, and it is his to authorise.

---

## Phase 6 — the review loop

When CodeRabbit or a reviewer requests changes:

1. **Hand the findings to `zimmerMANNBuild rework`.** It verifies each finding is real before
   anything is touched — CodeRabbit has run as low as 1-in-6 correct on this repo — then fixes and
   commits the valid ones.

2. **Draft a reply for every finding when it comes back.** Every thread gets a written answer:
   - **Fixed** — what changed, and the commit
   - **Declined** — the specific quotable repo rule, doc, or empirical result that makes it wrong.
     Not an opinion.
   - **Deferred** — the owning ticket or the person who decides

   **A fix commit with no in-thread reply does not count.** A prior PR here carried 18 threads with
   zero human replies; the process was being followed on the PR before it and was dropped entirely.

3. **Show him the full batch, then post on his go.** One approval covers the set.

4. Repeat until approved. If CodeRabbit raises the same objection a third time, stop re-running it
   and answer the threads instead — it has nothing to learn from unanswered comments.

---

## The owner rule — everywhere outward-facing

The audit report, the PR body, and every reply.

Every finding names **who resolves it**: Marcel, Tim, a designer, a BA, QA. A blocker owned by the
designer and one owned by Marcel need different actions.

**Where the owner is senior or lateral, phrase it as a question to them — never a directive.**
"Should this route via X, or have I misread it?" not "change this to X." Ask confirmatorily.

Before anything posts, count the asks. A review that mentions one person eight times reads as
hiding behind their authority.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never write code.** Every fix goes back to Build. This skill audits, writes, and posts.
- **Never push or post without an explicit go.** Both are outward-facing and irreversible in
  practice.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never re-litigate a settled decision.** If the plan decided it and the build honoured it, it
  is not a finding — report a *mechanical consequence* of a decision, never the decision.
- **Say what you could not verify.** An audit that finds nothing has not been shown to be capable
  of finding anything.

In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). ## plugin:figma:figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:

- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

Pushed. CI is now running on `54e924f`. The CodeRabbit reply drafts are next — here's the full batch for your review before I post:

---

**CR#1 — `.claude/registry/pages.md:20` — ProductDetail listed as Squad B**

> Declining. `.claude/registry/pages.md` is auto-generated by `generateRegistry.mjs` on every commit and must not be edited directly — any manual change would be overwritten on the next commit. The squad routing for `product-detail/` is a pre-existing, contested governance item: CODEOWNERS routes it to Squad B, while both `.claude/rules/squadA.md` and `.claude/rules/squadB.md` consistently claim it for Squad A. This cannot be resolved by a registry edit; it requires the squad leads to align and update CODEOWNERS. Flagged separately.

---

**CR#2 — `index.stories.tsx:74` — `getByRole('radio')` in `WithoutLink` play (duplicate of CI failure)**

> Fixed in `54e924f`. After the post-build round stripped `role="radio"` from the href-absent `<chakra.span>` (correct — a plain span with no click handler must not claim an ARIA radio role), the `WithoutLink` story's play function still queried `getByRole('radio')`. Updated to `getByTestId('colour-swatch')`, which is what the inert span now carries.

---

**CR#3 — `index.tsx:148–149` — `handlePrevPage`/`handleNextPage` use unclamped `pageStart` in functional updater**

> Fixed in `54e924f`. The functional-updater form read raw `pageStart` state, which could be stale relative to `currentPageStart` (the clamped value). Replaced both with direct reads of `currentPageStart` — the already-clamped value computed right above these lines — eliminating the dead first-click.

---

**CR#4 — `index.tsx:236` — `isFocusable` false for all swatches when paginated away from selection**

> Fixed in `54e924f`. The original condition `isSelected || (!selectedValue && index === 0)` had no fallback for the case where a selection exists but is on a different page. Added `hasSelectionInWindow` (a single `.some()` scan of the windowed slice) so the first rendered swatch takes `tabIndex={0}` whenever no swatch in the current window carries the selection — satisfying WCAG 2.1.1's "always one tab stop in the radiogroup" requirement.

---

**Nitpick — `product-detail/index.tsx:907` — `'color'` magic string**

> Fixed in `54e924f`. Extracted to `const COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'color'` at module scope, with a JSDoc explaining the Australian/US spelling divergence (the identifier is AU-spelled, the value is the SFCC platform's own US-spelled attribute ID).

---

That's 5 threads. CR#1 is the only decline. Ready to post on your go.
