# SFCC-91 — PreBuild gate (rev 2)

**Story:** PDP UI — Colour Swatches & Variation Selection
**Depth:** `standard` · **Run date:** 2026-08-31
**Repo state:** `develop` @ `269d5d4`, clean, level with origin
**Scope note:** run as a fresh build. Jhoan's branch and PR #70 deliberately ignored per instruction.

**Rev 2 changes:** Marcel supplied the ACs and 16 Figma node URLs — blockers #1, #2 and #3 are
**resolved**. One **new blocker** surfaced from the PRDs. Two earlier findings were **wrong** and
are corrected below.

---

## Verdict — ✅ CLEAR. All blockers resolved; plan written and handed off.

---

## Resolved since rev 1

| # | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 🔴 No acceptance criteria | **Resolved.** Five ACs supplied, covering swatch availability, single-colour text-label fallback, selected indication, selection behaviour, and unpopulated index images. |
| 2 | 🔴 Figma unresolvable | **Resolved — and my diagnosis was wrong.** I reported the files as returning stub pages under a View-seat restriction. That was incorrect: `get_metadata` without a node ID only lists top-level pages, and this file's page list is degenerate. Given node IDs, every node resolves. Access was never the problem. |
| 3 | 🔴 Design missing above 4 colours | **Resolved, and the design answers it concretely.** `40000307:13867` / `40001992:51882` each carry a `Pagination` frame (48×24, `Icon_chevron_left` + `Icon_chevron_right`) in the label row above a fixed 4-swatch window. **The >4 treatment is chevron pagination — not wrap, scroll, or "+N".** Icon dependency satisfied: `ChevronLeftIcon`/`ChevronRightIcon` already exist in `overrides/app/components/icons/zimm.tsx`. |
| 13 | Dependency on SFCC-89 | Confirmed cleared — PR #64 merged 2026-08-27. |

---

## 🔴 The remaining blocker

| # | Source | Finding | Severity | What unblocks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 19 | `.docs/prd/` | **Both PRDs say do not build this yet.** `.docs/prd/plp.md` §5.4 (SPR-26 — Open): *"colour swatch creation and management in Business Manager — map colour attribute values… to hex code or swatch image… Colour mapping exercise TBC. **Do not implement until confirmed.**"* Repeated in `.docs/prd/pdp.md:219` Open Items: *"Colour swatch management and mapping — colour mapping exercise TBC (SPR-26, PRD-004)."* And `.docs/prd/pdp.md:17` (PRD-002, confirmed): *"Colour swatch assets do not live in AP21 — only colour names."* The Jira ACs instruct the opposite. | 🔴 BLOCKED | Per AGENTS.md *Doc integrity*: cite the doc, stop, and ask whether the PRD is now stale (SPR-26 resolved by the BM index-image decision) or whether the ticket is running ahead of it. Not a call to make silently. |

---

## 🟡 Clarify / informational

| # | Source | Finding | Severity | What unblocks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | AC vs codebase | ~~The AC's swatch source and the base implementation disagree.~~ **RESOLVED — verified against the live dev API 2026-08-31.** `viewType: 'swatch'` exists and is populated. The per-colour swatch group (carrying `variationAttributes: color=[...]`, which is what base `getVariantValueSwatch`'s filter needs) appears **only when `allImages=true`** — and `pages/product-detail/index.tsx:220` already passes it on the main `useProduct`. No fetch change needed; no new exposure to the `allImages` behaviour recorded under SFCC-29. **This is a styling story, not a data story.** | ✅ RESOLVED | — |
| 5 | Confluence / Jira | ~~PRD-004 is split and only half is deliverable.~~ **RESOLVED by the ACs.** AC 4 specifies the URL updating *without* full page reload — that is the same-master variant switch, which is this story. SFCC-708 covers *cross-master* related colours with different style codes (products that are not natural variants of one master). The split is clean and the ACs state this story's half explicitly. | ✅ RESOLVED | — |
| 4 | Confluence | **PARTLY resolved — I closed this too fast earlier.** AC 1 supersedes PRD-004's wording for the **single-colour** case (`Colour: Bay Blue`, not "Only available in"). But PRD-004's *"Also available in"* applies to the **cross-SKU** case, which is real and still live — just deferred to SFCC-708. Verified 2026-08-31: the product API exposes only `c_careInstructions` and `c_sizeFit`, so no related-colours attribute exists yet, which is why the AC was moved out on 2026-08-12. **Design gap:** the Figma `labelContainer` (`40000307:13867`) holds two text nodes sizing to `"Colour:"` + value — there is no "Also available in" label variant anywhere in the design. | 🟡 CLARIFY → **SFCC-708** | Design needs to specify the group label for the cross-SKU case before SFCC-708 builds it. Not blocking SFCC-91. |
| 8 | CODEOWNERS | **Cross-squad, and squad ownership of the PDP is itself contested.** `swatch-group/` → Squad B + tier-2 + tier-1 (`CODEOWNERS:103`, Tier 2). `pages/product-detail/` → Squad B (`CODEOWNERS:162`) — but `.claude/rules/squadA.md:4,34` claims it for Squad A. The ticket is labelled `Squad-A`. | 🟡 CLARIFY | CODEOWNERS is authoritative for review routing; the squadA.md conflict is a separate governance item. |
| 9 | Confluence | **Design tracker vs ticket.** 04.72 records PDP components finalised **Aug 13** under an explicit *"once locked, no further design changes are permitted"* rule, yet design was pending on Aug 26. The tracker's PDP scope also never lists a colour swatch. | 🟡 CLARIFY | Raise as process drift; does not block this build now that nodes exist. |

---

## 🔵 Notes

| # | Source | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| 21 | Figma | **The design's variants do not match the base component's.** `pdp/product-colour-picker` (`40000307:13823`) ships **two sizes × three states**: `Large/Rectangle` (48×72) and `Small/Rounded` (20×24), each in `Unselected` / `Selected` / `Focus`. Base `Swatch` offers `square` \| `circle`. A 48×72 portrait rectangle is not a square and a 20×24 rounded rect is not a circle — so the recipe needs its own variant vocabulary, not the base's. |
| 22 | Figma | **No Hover and no Disabled state exist in the design** — and both absences are *correct*. `.docs/prd/pdp.md:17` states hover-to-preview is *"a custom build, not OOTB, and not scoped for go-live"*; and the AC handles unpopulated variations by **not rendering them**, so no disabled state is needed. The design is internally consistent with the PRD here. |
| 23 | Figma | **Placement is fixed.** `Colour Options` sits inside `Content Card and Colour Swatch` at y=126 (218×104), between the product description and the size selector — `40000307:14062`. The PDP content column also carries `Default` / `Warning` / `Unavailable` / `Coming soon` states at desktop **and** mobile. |
| 18 | Codebase | **CORRECTION to rev 1.** I framed the recipe name as a judgement call. It is not — it is mechanically enforced. `recipeGuards.test.ts:351` sets `INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']` and its comment reads *"Anything else must be namespaced (e.g. ZimmFooter, not Footer)."* Base SFCC registers a `SwatchGroup` recipe, so a key literally named `SwatchGroup` would deep-merge the base and **fail `npm run test`**. Name it **`ZimmSwatchGroup`**. |
| 10 | Codebase | **CORRECTION to rev 1.** I reported that base `Swatch` selects on hover at `lg`+ and implied it affects the PDP. It does not. `swatch.jsx:69` applies the hover handlers only when there is no `href` (`{...(href ? {} : selectHandlers)}`), and `use-variation-attributes.js:152-153` sets `href: null` only in *controlled* mode — the quick-view modals. On the PDP path `href` is a real URL, so swatches are `RouteLink`s and hover-select never fires. Live in quick-view modals only. |
| 11 | Codebase | Base `disabled` is **visual only** — fed to `useMultiStyleConfig` at `swatch.jsx:35`, never spread onto the `<Button>`; no `isDisabled`, no `aria-disabled`, no click guard. Not triggered by this story's ACs (unpopulated variants are not rendered), but PRD-014's disabled *size* swatch will hit it. |
| 15 | Codebase | **Dormant landmine — only if `swatch-group` is overridden.** `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:71-72` imports the swatch by base path. The moment an override exists, those must become `'../swatch-group'` / `'../swatch-group/swatch'` or Storybook and Vitest silently exercise the **base** component. The render-slot architecture sidesteps this entirely. |
| 24 | Codebase | Base recipe `theme/components/project/swatch-group.js` declares `parts: ['swatch','swatchButton']` while its `baseStyle` carries five keys — the exact undeclared-parts defect `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts:101` exists to catch. Declare every part you read. |
| 25 | Docs | **Doc drift.** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:129-132` cites `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice` import as a "known instance, not yet fixed" — but `overrides/app/components/product-tile/` **does not exist on develop**. |
| 16 | Codebase | On `develop`; the `PreToolUse` hook blocks writes there. `feature/SFCC-91_pdp-ui-colour-swatches-variation-selection` already exists on origin (Jhoan's) — a fresh branch needs a different name. |
| 17 | Docs | `.docs/memory/projectState.md` last updated 2026-08-24; `sprintScope.md` still reads *"Sprint 0 — Foundation"*. Don't scope from either. |

---

## Recommended architecture — a render slot, not a `swatch-group` override

The strongest option, and it dissolves findings #7 and #15 rather than managing them.

Commit `227171e` added `renderHeader?: (props) => React.ReactNode` to the `product-view` override —
a **render slot on the default export**, defaulting to the base behaviour exactly. Its message
argues the case directly:

> *"overrideStyling.md prescribes putting Zimmermann-only additions behind a named export that
> wraps the default. That route cannot express this requirement: a wrapper can only set props the
> default already accepts, so letting a caller replace an internal render block still requires the
> slot on the default. The only alternative is forking the component body, which is a graver
> breach of the faithful-port rule."*

A `renderVariationAttributes` slot is the direct analogue. It means:

- **No `swatch-group` override** → PLP and the recommendations carousels are untouched.
- **No Tier 2 / Squad B file** in the diff, and no cross-squad approval gate.
- **No import-path landmine** (#15) to create and then have to remember.
- A new `ZimmColourSwatch` / `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` in `ui-kits/`, following the
  `zimmProduct*` four-file pattern established by PR #64.

The alternative — a faithful `swatch-group` port plus a `ZimmSwatchGroup` recipe — is the
conventional route, but it changes PLP and every carousel, and needs Squad B plus Tier 2 sign-off.

---

## The build pattern (from PR #64 / SFCC-89, the nearest in-kind precedent)

Four files per component, mirroring `ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductStyleCode/`:
`index.tsx` · `index.stories.tsx` · `index.test.tsx` · `<name>.css.ts`, plus one line in
`overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`.

- Recipe key hoisted to a module const; `useMultiStyleConfig(KEY, {...})`.
- Styling applied via `<chakra.x __css={styles.part}>` — never `sx` or style props.
- **`var(--zimm-*)` belongs in the `.css.ts` recipe, not in JSX.** Verified: 17 recipe files use it;
  exactly one component `.tsx` does (`footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44,62`), and only inside a
  `__css={{...styles.part, ...conditional}}` spread the recipe cannot express.
- `textStyle` set in the recipe, and it stays a bare key — there is no `var()` substitute for the
  composite expansion.
- Hooks above any early return; `const intl = useIntl()` then `intl.formatMessage(...)` (never
  destructured — `@typescript-eslint/unbound-method`).
- Labels via `react-intl`, **not** `useUiCopy` — `useContentful.ts` sends no `locale`, so `uiCopy`
  would serve the space default to all 8 storefronts.
- Two hard gates on `npm run test`: `recipeParts.test.ts:101` (declared parts must cover every
  `styles.*` read) and `recipeGuards.test.ts` (6 guards, incl. bare-token and namespacing).
- Story title `Commerce/Zimm<Name>`; a `play` where there is interactive behaviour.

**No hook override.** All variation logic funnels through `useDerivedProduct` →
`useVariationAttributes` → `useVariationParams`, and `product-view` already receives decorated
`variationAttributes`. Overriding a hook routes through the `hooks/index.js` barrel, which resolves
in the app build but **not** in Storybook or Vitest.

---

## What was not checked

- **`/feature-spec` and `/scope-check` not run** — deferred until blocker #19 is answered, since
  the answer changes whether there is a story to scope at all.
- **Zephyr** — no test-case lookup for SFCC-91.
- **`get_design_context`** — metadata only so far; exact tokens, spacing and type per state still
  to be pulled from the 16 nodes at plan time.
- **No build or test was run.** Every codebase claim is read from source. `audit:tokens` is known
  to carry ~14 pre-existing findings.

---

## Provenance

- Jira SFCC-91 (ACs supplied by Marcel), SFCC-708 (`Ready for Development`, not started)
- Figma `Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` — `40001992:51881`, `40000307:13823`, `40000307:14062`,

| `npm run build-storybook` | Exit 0, succeeded | — |
| `npm run test:max-file-size` | **2 checks passed** — `main.js` 114.39KB < 180KB, `vendor.js` 515.02KB < 550KB | — |
| `npm run test:story` (BrowserStack) | **Did not run** — `BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME`, `BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY`, `RETAIL_APP_HOME`, `PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL`, `PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD` are present as keys in `.env` but all five values are empty. Local environment gap, not a code issue. | — |
| `cr review --light --base develop` | 4 findings — 1 fixed (`2d8a9a7`), 3 investigated and not actioned (2 false positives, 1 pre-existing repo-wide gap out of this story's scope) | — |
| Marcel's dev-server visual check (Step 4, AC 4 + 4 other points) | **Passed** — confirmed no white-flash/full-reload on swatch click, correct visual states, and confirmed no live set/bundle product currently has colour-variant children | — |

## CodeRabbit findings — disposition (for whoever handles the real PR-level review; these were investigated now so the reasoning is ready, not re-derived)

1. **Fixed** (`2d8a9a7`) — `product-view/index.tsx`'s `renderVariationAttribute` JSDoc said `??` "only" treats `undefined` as absent, then said `null` also falls through — a literal contradiction. Corrected.
2. **Not actionable as proposed; reveals a real, pre-existing, repo-wide gap.** Flagged the two new pagination `aria-label` message IDs as absent from `translations/*.json`. True, but `translations/en-US.json` is a **generated** file (`translations/README.md`), extracted via `npm run extract-default-translations` (`formatjs extract`). Verified directly: running that extraction added *nothing* — confirmed by declaring the message as a module-level const referenced by variable name at the call site (`intl.formatMessage(PREVIOUS_PAGE_MESSAGE)`), which `formatjs extract`'s static analysis cannot resolve (it needs an inline literal or `defineMessages()`). Verified this is **not new**: `zimmProductStyleCode`'s already-committed `LABEL_MESSAGE` uses the identical pattern and **also** has zero occurrences in `translations/en-US.json`. Every custom Zimmermann-authored i18n message in this codebase has this gap, not just this story's two. Worth its own investigation — out of SFCC-91's scope.
3. **Real, but already investigated and deliberately deferred during Step 2's own build**, not a new SFCC-91 regression. `ZimmColourSwatch`'s `href`-absent branch (`chakra.span role="radio"`) has no `onClick`/`onKeyDown` at all — confirmed even worse than CodeRabbit's framing (neither Enter nor Space nor a click does anything, not just "Space is missing"; base SFCC's own equivalent renders a real `<button>` here, which gets both natively for free). This path is the quick-view-modal case and has zero callers anywhere in the app today (`product-detail`'s main `<ProductView>` passes no `controlledVariationValues`) — confirmed at Step 2's original build and re-confirmed here. Tracked, not fixed now.
4. **False positive.** Claimed `v.image` isn't the "index image" `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` expects. Traced directly: `useVariationAttributes` sets `value.image = getVariantValueSwatch(product, value)` (`use-variation-attributes.js:150`), and `getVariantValueSwatch`'s entire purpose — filtering `imageGroups` on `viewType: 'swatch'` for that colour — **is** SFCC's own resolution of the BM-designated index image (matches Jira's own ticket description verbatim). `v.image` already is the index image before Step 4's code ever touches it.

## UNIFORM findings (recur across steps or the wider codebase — not one-offs)

- **`recipeGuards.test.ts`'s exhaustive fuzzing walk only varies five hardcoded boolean keys** (`inverse, disabled, hasError, focused, filled`). Any new state-dependent recipe prop outside that set is silently never exercised by the hard styling gate. Hit **twice** in this build — `ZimmColourSwatch`'s `selected` (Step 2) and `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s `isPaginated` (Step 3). Both branches were manually verified token-clean, but the automated backstop doesn't see either. `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` is Tier 2 (UI-designer-owned), out of this build's scope to change.
- **`audit:tokens`/similar checks validate a `var(--zimm-*)` string is well-formed, never that the name is real.** Root cause of Step 2's first rework round — `var(--zimm-color-background-02)` (fabricated, plausible-looking, doesn't exist) passed every gate including the component's own regression test, because jsdom echoes back whatever string is declared without resolving it. Only a real-Chromium render caught it.
- **No custom Zimmermann-authored i18n message has ever reached the translation extraction pipeline** (see CodeRabbit finding 2 above) — confirmed repo-wide, not new to this story.
- **`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` never scans `overrides/app/pages/**`** — only `overrides/app/components/**` and `overrides/app/theme/components/**`. Moot for this build (no styling literals landed in `product-detail/index.tsx`), but a real gap for any future page-level styling work.

## Could not verify

- **BrowserStack story run** — blocked on empty local credentials, never executed. Needs `.env` populated per `.env.sample`, then `npm run test:story` re-run.
- **`attr.name` empty-string edge case** (`?? ''` fallback in Step 4's mapping) — `VariationAttribute.name` is genuinely optional at the real SDK contract level, and `label=""` is not exercised anywhere in `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s own test suite. Not proven to occur with Zimmermann's real catalog data; no live BM access this build to confirm either way.
- **Whether the label-group's static "Colour:" text needing no dedicated recipe part is the right long-term call** — judged defensible (static, non-interactive, no competing style definitions) but not confirmed with a designer.

## Outstanding

- **Set/bundle child products' colour variation attributes still render the old base swatch UI**, not `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` — confirmed real and reachable in generic SFCC data (base mock fixtures), out of SFCC-91's stated scope (ticket and ACs are standalone-PDP only), no confirmed Figma treatment for that layout context exists. Marcel confirmed no live product currently exercises this, so it is not a live inconsistency today — needs its own ticket if/when Zimmermann's catalog adds one, and that ticket should start by asking whether a Figma design exists for a set/bundle child's colour picker before anyone builds it.
- **AC 4 (URL updates without full reload) has no automated E2E coverage.** Verified manually by Marcel on a real dev server; a `pdp`-area Playwright spec would need its own `.feature` file (Lead QA sign-off first) and a new allow-list group in `qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` (Tier 1 CI config) — both out of this build's scope.
- **`.docs/prd/plp.md` §5.4 and `pdp.md:219`** still read "Do not implement until confirmed" (SPR-26) — Marcel ruled this stale during PreBuild, but the docs themselves haven't been corrected. Human-only edit (skills are barred from `.docs/prd/**`).
- **The i18n extraction gap** (see UNIFORM findings) is worth its own investigation — potentially affects every custom Zimmermann message across the whole codebase, not just this story's two.
- **`Small/Rounded` swatch variant** was scoped out entirely (no border-radius token exists in Tier 1 `theme/foundation/`, no consumer) — a decision, not a gap, but flagging so it isn't silently rediscovered.

## Repo state

`git status` clean. Nothing pushed. No PR opened. Working tree also carries a **pre-existing, unrelated, uncommitted translation diff** (`translations/en-GB.json`, `translations/en-US.json`, `overrides/app/static/translations/compiled/{en-GB,en-US,en-XA}.json` — adds `header.button.assistive_msg.search` and a `Quantity:` string, unrelated to SFCC-91, most likely stray local state from the in-progress header rebuild on a different branch). Confirmed this predates this build's own work and is untouched by it — left exactly as found, not staged, not committed.

content.text:
Both fan-out agents are done, and I've independently re-verified the one claim the whole thing hinges on. Confirmed directly: base's `getDecoratedVariationAttributes` (`product-utils.js:218-239`) does a plain `.map()` over every variation value with no `.filter()` at all — every colour, orderable or not, image or not, gets decorated and handed to `SwatchGroup`, which renders unavailable ones as disabled squares rather than withholding them. That's the mechanism behind the AC5 bug both agents traced independently. Full picture below.

## Gate table — head (`f9c6c74`) vs. base (`04039a9`)

| Gate | Base | Head | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | 0 errors | 0 errors | clean |
| `npm run test` | 25 files / 379 tests | 27 files / 407 tests, all passing | clean, real growth |
| `npm run lint` | 19 problems (4 err/15 warn) | 30 problems (13 err/17 warn) | **+9 errors, +2 warnings — all in this PR's own files, none pre-existing** |
| `audit:tokens` | 4 unacknowledged | 4 unacknowledged, identical set | clean, no regression |

CodeRabbit approved on 2026-08-28 after Jhoan's own six fix rounds. **Tim (human reviewer) then requested changes** on 2026-08-28 22:06 — after her last commit — with one still-unresolved thread that tags you directly, asking whether the swatch images need real alt text.

## Findings, ranked by cost of ignoring

**1. 🔴 AC5 is broken for the "all colours unavailable" case — CONFIRMED three ways now.** `suppressColourAttribute={hasOfferedColour}` (`product-detail/index.tsx:905`) goes `false` whenever every colour is withheld, which un-suppresses the base swatch loop — and that loop has no filtering at all (just verified above), so it renders every unavailable colour as a disabled square. This directly contradicts the PR's own Gherkin scenario ("no colour label or swatches are displayed"). Nothing in the delivered test suite catches it — `product-detail/index.tsx` has no unit test file, and the one E2E scenario written for exactly this case can't run (next finding). Fix is narrow: gate on `colourVariants.length > 0`, not `hasOfferedColour`.

**2. 🔴 The entire new Playwright suite is non-functional — confirmed by executing it, not reading it.** The spec imports five fixture functions (`pdpProductWithMultipleColours`, etc.) that don't exist in `e2e/fixtures/products.js` — calling one throws `TypeError` before any `test.skip` guard is reached. It also calls ~10 page-object methods/properties on `ProductPage.js` that were never added. 10 of 11 tests error out immediately; the 11th has no skip guard and would fail for real. The PR body's claim — "all 11 scenarios skip, not a merge blocker" — is factually wrong on both counts. The Gherkin itself is well-written and would catch real regressions once the plumbing exists.

**3. 🔴 `variant="square"` is a real, undisclosed regression outside this ticket's scope.** Confirmed: it's unconditional, not gated behind the suppression flag, so it changes swatch shape (circle → square) in cart quick-add, wishlist, bonus-product (Squad A's territory), and the PDP's own set/bundle children — none named in SFCC-91. Zero existing tests catch it; no commit or doc cites a design decision for it. The introducing commit's own message claims the opposite effect.

**4. 🟡 The branch is 13 commits behind `develop` and GitHub marks it `CONFLICTING`.** It predates the already-merged SFCC-194 (Was/Now price) story. The real conflict lands exactly where both stories touch `renderHeader` → `StaticProductHeader` — needs a careful manual merge that keeps both `afterContent` (colour) and `isPriceLoading`/`priceData` (Was/Now), not a mechanical pick of one side.

**5. 🟡 `filterImageGroups.ts` reimplements a function the base package already exports — and the PR's own sibling files prove it.** `product-view/index.tsx` and `product-detail/index.tsx` both already import other functions from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils` in this same PR. The new file's header comment claims the base version "has no public export," which is false — confirmed directly against the package source. The reimplementation also has a real (if currently harmless) null-handling divergence from the base version, and no test file despite having conditional branches, which `conventions.md` requires.

**6. 🟡 Disabled chevron uses `opacity: 0.3`, not a colour token.** You specifically ruled on this for the other build after checking Figma directly (`stroke: var(--alias-color-icon-disabled, ...)`) — a colour-based treatment, not opacity. Worth a direct Figma check to confirm which is actually right.

**7. 🟡 Swatch dimensions disagree between the two builds.** Hers: 47×72px, image aspect ratio 36:55. The other build: 48×72px, ratio 2:3. These aren't the same value expressed differently — one of the two Figma reads is off by a meaningful amount. Worth settling directly against Figma.

**8. 🟡 AC5's scope itself may be under-specified in both builds.** Her filter also excludes non-orderable colours, citing a BA conversation dated 2026-08-21. That decision doesn't appear to have reached Jira or Confluence — the other build's PreBuild found no such requirement. Either she has a real requirement the other build missed, or it's an uncaptured decision that needs to go back into the ticket properly.

**9. 🔵 Pagination logic has zero test coverage.** Every fixture in both the Vitest suite and Storybook uses ≤3 variants, so the 4-swatch page boundary, chevron clicks, and the deep-link-to-a-later-page effect are never exercised. A comment in the test file claims Storybook's interaction tests "fail on every story in the repo" as the justification — disproven directly; they were run locally and pass.

**10. 🔵 An unrelated translation key landed in 2 of 4 locale files** (`header.button.assistive_msg.search`, belonging to a file this PR never touches). Worth noting fairly: our own build's `handoff.md` flagged the identical stray key sitting uncommitted in that session's working tree, most likely from an in-progress header rebuild on a different branch. This reads like shared local dev-state leakage, not deliberate scope creep on her part.

**11. 🔵 9 new lint errors / 2 new warnings**, precisely attributed to this PR's own files — mostly auto-fixable prettier formatting, but two are real rule violations (`@typescript-eslint/unbound-method`, `@typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-type-assertion`).

## Scope verdict

**OVER** — reaches outside the ticket's boundary without disclosure (`variant="square"`, the stray translation key) *and* silently under-delivers named commitments (the E2E suite, the AC5 edge case) at the same time. Tier check is clean otherwise — no Tier 1 touched, and the Tier 2 `theme/components/index.ts` edit is registration-only, correctly handled.

## What nobody verified

The `hasOfferedColour` bug's real-browser behaviour (traced statically through three files including the base package — high confidence, not click-tested live). Whether CI's `storybook-test` job passes for this PR specifically (spot-checked 3 of ~30 stories locally, all pass). Whether BrowserStack's Jira-tag scoping would even attempt this spec pre-merge.

---

# zimmerMANNReview — PR #74 (Marcel's own build)

Branch: `feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches`   Head: `54e924f`   Base: `269d5d4`
Reviewed: 2026-08-31   Reviewer: Marcel (FED Lead), via zimmerMANNReview

**Scope note:** same requirements ground truth as `review-pr70.md` (Jira/Confluence/Figma
lookups skipped, this build's own `plan.md`/`findings.md`/`handoff.md`/`postbuild.md` used
instead). This is a **second, independent pass** on top of PostBuild's own self-audit — run with
the specific defect classes just found in PR #70 in mind, as a comparative check.

**Status: findings gathered and held. Nothing posted anywhere.**

---

## Gate table — head (`54e924f`) vs. base (`269d5d4`)

| Gate | Base | Head | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | 0 errors | 0 errors | clean |
| `npm run test` | 26 files / 408 tests | 28 files / 433 tests, all passing | clean, real growth |
| `npm run lint` | 20 problems (4 err/16 warn) | 22 problems (6 err/16 warn) | **+2 errors, +0 warnings — both trivial prettier formatting** |
| `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` | 4 unacknowledged | 4 unacknowledged, identical set | clean, no regression |

Full lint attribution at head, verified line-by-line against base: all pre-existing
warnings/errors (`header/index.tsx` ×3, `product-view/index.tsx` ×7, `zimmContactIconRow/
index.stories.tsx` ×1, `product-detail/index.tsx` ×5, `routes.tsx` ×2, `recipeGuards.test.ts` ×2)
are identical in count and type, just line-shifted. Exactly 2 new errors, both auto-fixable
prettier formatting from the Round 1 fix commit: `zimmColourSwatch/index.test.tsx:119` (a
reformatted multi-line JSX call) and `zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx:86` (a collapsed single-line
span). **Dramatically cleaner than PR #70's +9 errors/+2 warnings for the equivalent comparison.**

CI: fully green (all checks pass, including Storybook interaction/a11y). CodeRabbit auto-approved
after the Round 1 fix round ("Comments resolved. Approval completed"). No human review yet. PR
title corrected, still in draft.

---

## Findings — checked specifically against the defect classes found in PR #70

### 1. 🟡 The "zero offered colours" edge case is handled differently, and is unverified against a real requirement — but does not have PR #70's bug

Traced the equivalent path: `renderVariationAttribute` always renders `<ZimmColourSwatchGroup>`
whenever `attr.id === 'color'` exists at all (`product-detail/index.tsx:914`), regardless of
whether any colour has a resolved image. Inside `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`
(`zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx`), the **label row renders unconditionally** — only the
swatches row is gated (`populated.length > 1`). So when every colour lacks an image,
`populated.length` is `0`, no swatches render, but "Colour: `<SFCC's own selectedValue name>`"
still shows.

This is **documented, deliberate behaviour**, not an accident: `plan.md` §7 assumptions states
directly — "Zero populated colours falls back to the text label for the selected colour rather
than rendering nothing: the shopper still needs to know what they're viewing." But it is also
explicitly flagged there as **unconfirmed with anyone** ("Not confirmed by anyone" applies to the
neighbouring assumption; this one has no BA/PM sign-off recorded either).

**Compared with PR #70:** her intended behaviour for this exact case (per her own Gherkin) is to
hide the colour section entirely — a different, but equally unconfirmed-against-a-written-AC,
design choice. The difference that matters: **her code doesn't achieve her own stated intent**
(it falls through to a broken disabled-squares render, finding 1 in `review-pr70.md`), while our
code does exactly what its own documented assumption says it will do. Neither is proven to match
the real, singular business requirement — this needs a BA/PM answer, not a code fix, and the
answer likely applies to both PRs identically.

### 2. 🔴 Non-orderable colours are not filtered, not disabled, not distinguished at all — confirmed, and this is the mirror image of PR #70's bug

`product-detail/index.tsx:919-924`'s mapping passes `{value, name, href, imageUrl}` only — no
`orderable` field anywhere. `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s only filter is
`Boolean(value.imageUrl)` (`zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx`, the `populated` filter) — no
orderable check. `ZimmColourSwatch`'s prop surface (`{name, imageUrl, href, isSelected,
isFocusable}`) has **no `disabled` prop at all**.

**Practical consequence, confirmed by reading the full render path:** a colour that is out of
stock but still has a resolved swatch image renders as a completely normal, fully clickable,
undifferentiated swatch — no visual distinction from an available colour, and clicking it would
attempt to select an unorderable variant.

This was flagged as a known, accepted gap during PreBuild (`findings.md` #11: "Base disabled is
visual only... Not triggered by this story's ACs... but PRD-014's disabled *size* swatch will
hit it") — but that finding predicted the gap for the **size** attribute, not colour. **PR #70's
own code cites a BA conversation dated 2026-08-21 establishing that non-orderable *colours*
specifically should be withheld entirely** — ten days before this build's own PreBuild ran, and
that decision doesn't appear to have been surfaced during this build's Jira/Confluence sweep.

If that BA decision is real and current, this build is **under-scoped on AC5** in exactly the
dimension PR #70 (badly) attempted to cover: this build simply doesn't attempt orderable-filtering
at all, where PR #70 attempted it and got the implementation wrong. Same open question as
`review-pr70.md` finding 8 — needs a BA/PM answer, and the answer determines a real follow-up
fix on **this** build too, not just a note on the other PR.

### 3. ✅ No `variant="square"`-equivalent scope creep — confirmed clean

This build's architecture (a `renderVariationAttribute` render slot, entirely separate from the
base swatch-rendering loop) never touches `product-view/index.tsx`'s existing swatch-variant
logic at all — confirmed directly: `git diff 269d5d4..HEAD -- overrides/app/components/product-
view/index.tsx` shows only the new slot prop, its JSDoc, and the call-site wiring; the
`variant={id === 'color' ? 'circle' : 'square'}` line is untouched. Cart, wishlist, bonus-product,
and this PDP's own set/bundle children all keep rendering circle swatches for colour exactly as
before. This class of defect does not exist here — a direct benefit of the render-slot
architecture over a shared-loop-modification approach.

### 4. ✅ No `filterImageGroups`-equivalent reimplementation — confirmed correct, already verified in the original build

This build never needed a new image-filtering utility: `v.image` (from
`useVariationAttributes` → base `getVariantValueSwatch`) already **is** the resolved index image
by the time Step 4's mapping code runs — confirmed at the time by tracing
`use-variation-attributes.js:150` and `getVariantValueSwatch`'s own filter logic (recorded in
`handoff.md`'s CodeRabbit-finding-4 disposition, itself independently re-verified this session by
reading the same base source). No DRY violation, no duplicate logic, no false comment about a
"missing" public export — because nothing was reimplemented in the first place.

### 5. ✅ E2E coverage gap is honestly disclosed — does not repeat PR #70's false claim

`handoff.md` and `postbuild.md` both state plainly: "AC 4 (URL updates without full reload) has
no automated E2E coverage... verified manually by Marcel on a real dev server." No `.feature`
file, no Playwright spec, and — critically — **no claim anywhere that tests exist and merely
skip**. This is the opposite failure mode from PR #70's spec (which claims comprehensive coverage
that turns out to be entirely non-functional). This build's gap is smaller in raw coverage but
larger in honesty: what's stated to exist, exists; what doesn't, is named as missing.

### 6. 🟡 Disabled chevron colour — confirmed correct against a real Figma check, unlike PR #70's

`zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`'s `pageButton._disabled` uses
`color: 'var(--zimm-color-icon-disabled)'` — a colour-based treatment. Unlike the swatch-
dimension question below, **this one has a direct, first-party confirmation**: Marcel personally
supplied the exact Figma style for this element earlier in this build (`stroke-width: 1px;
stroke: var(--alias-color-icon-disabled, #D1D1D1);`), and the token was built to match it exactly
(`--zimm-color-icon-disabled` → `grey[200]` → `#d1d1d1`). PR #70's equivalent
(`colourSwatches.css.ts:61`, `opacity: 0.3`) does not match this confirmed spec. On this one
point, this build is verified correct where the other isn't — not a symmetric open question.

### 7. 🟡 Swatch dimensions still an open, symmetric question

This build: 48px width (`var(--zimm-scale-1200)`), `aspectRatio: '2 / 3'` (yields 72px height).
PR #70: 47px width, `aspectRatio: '36 / 55'`. Both trace to Figma reads taken independently (this
build's `plan.md` Step 2, four days after PR #70's commits) — neither has the kind of direct,
Marcel-confirmed resolution that the chevron colour does. Genuinely unresolved; needs a fresh
Figma check, not resolvable by comparing the two PRs' own citations against each other.

### 8. 🔵 Minor: empty `attr.values` edge case, low real-world likelihood

If SFCC ever returned a `color` attribute with zero `values` (not observed, not expected in
practice), `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` would render "Colour:" with an empty/undefined name and no
swatches — no crash, just a slightly odd label. Far lower severity than PR #70's equivalent case
since it requires a malformed API response rather than a normal, real-world "all sold out"
product state.

---

## Comparative summary

| Defect class found in PR #70 | Present in PR #74? |
|---|---|
| AC5 broken for "all colours unavailable" (renders broken disabled squares) | No — renders a text label instead (undocumented-with-BA, but not broken) |
| Non-functional E2E suite, falsely claimed as "skip pending fixtures" | No — gap is real but honestly disclosed as missing, not claimed as built |
| Undisclosed `variant="square"` cross-surface regression | No — architecture never touches the shared swatch loop |
| Reimplemented base utility with a false "no export" justification | No — reused the base-resolved image directly, no reimplementation |
| Disabled-chevron treatment not matching confirmed Figma spec | No — colour-token treatment matches Marcel's direct Figma confirmation |
| Non-orderable colours not filtered/distinguished | **Yes, in the opposite direction** — not filtered at all (vs. PR #70's filtered-but-buggy-fallback) |
| Swatch dimension/aspect-ratio uncertainty | **Yes, symmetrically** — both builds have an independent, unconfirmed Figma read |
| Stray unrelated translation key | No — not present in this build's diff |
| Branch staleness / merge conflict with SFCC-194 | No — this branch is current with develop, `MERGEABLE` |

**Net read:** this build avoids every *proven, executable* defect class found in PR #70 — largely
as a structural consequence of the render-slot architecture not touching shared code paths, and
of PostBuild's own prior self-audit having already caught the DRY/token/WCAG issues that
would otherwise parallel PR #70's findings. The two real open items are **not code defects**, they're
**the same missing requirement answer** (does AC5 need to filter non-orderable colours?) surfacing
on both PRs from opposite directions — PR #70 attempted it and got the wiring wrong; this build
never attempted it at all. Whichever way that answer goes, it is very likely a real, additional
follow-up needed on **this** build, not a clean pass to wave through silently.

## What nobody verified

- The zero-populated-colours text-label behaviour (finding 1) and the non-orderable-colour gap
  (finding 2) against a live product shaped exactly this way — both traced statically through the
  full render path, not click-tested against a real SFCC product.
- The swatch dimension/aspect-ratio question (finding 7) — needs a live Figma check, not
  resolvable by comparing the two PRs' citations.

1	import React from 'react';
2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	import { Link as RouteLink } from 'react-router-dom';
4	
5	const ZIMM_COLOUR_SWATCH_RECIPE = 'ZimmColourSwatch';
6	
7	// Same import base SFCC's own swatch-group/swatch.jsx uses for its `RouteLink` — a router
8	// `Link` is what actually delivers "URL updates without a full page reload": it pushes history
9	// rather than navigating the document. There is no overrides/.../link equivalent to reuse
10	// instead — confirmed none exists for this.
11	const ColourSwatchLink = chakra(RouteLink);
12	
13	type ZimmColourSwatchProps = {
14	  /** Colour display name. Not rendered as visible text — used as the accessible name (`aria-label`). */
15	  name: string;
16	  /**
17	   * Fully resolved image URL for this colour's swatch fill. Resolution is the caller's job —
18	   * this component performs no SFCC-shape lookup of its own.
19	   */
20	  imageUrl: string;
21	  /**
22	   * Destination URL for this colour variation. Absent for the quick-view-modal path, where
23	   * SFCC's own `useVariationAttributes` returns `href: null` and the swatch must not navigate.
24	   */
25	  href?: string;
26	  /** Whether this is the currently selected colour. */
27	  isSelected: boolean;
28	  /**
29	   * Whether this swatch is reachable via Tab (`tabIndex={0}`) vs. removed from the tab order
30	   * (`tabIndex={-1}`) — the caller drives a roving tabindex across the swatch group.
31	   */
32	  isFocusable: boolean;
33	};
34	
35	/**
36	 * Atom — a single colour swatch in a PDP colour-variation list: a clickable rectangle filled
37	 * with that colour's product photo, radio semantics (one selection out of the group), and a
38	 * router `Link` when a destination URL exists so selecting a colour updates the URL without a
39	 * full page reload.
40	 *
41	 * Purely presentational — no data-fetching hook of any kind. SFCC data resolution (building
42	 * `imageUrl`/`href` from a product's variation attributes) happens at the page level, not this
43	 * atom.
44	 */
45	export const ZimmColourSwatch = ({ name, imageUrl, href, isSelected, isFocusable }: ZimmColourSwatchProps) => {
46	  // Above any early return — there isn't one here, this component always renders something.
47	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_COLOUR_SWATCH_RECIPE, { selected: isSelected });
48	
49	  // The dynamic URL genuinely cannot live in the static recipe file, so this one dynamic `__css`
50	  // spread is the correct, deliberate exception — the same shape already used at
51	  // footer/footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44 and :62, an established pattern in this codebase.
52	  const image = <chakra.span __css={{ ...styles.image, backgroundImage: `url(${imageUrl})` }} />;
53	
54	  /*
55	   * Deliberately no `backgroundColor={name.toLowerCase()}` here, unlike base SFCC's own
56	   * `renderDefaultVariationAttribute` (product-view/index.jsx, and our own extraction of it in
57	   * product-view/index.tsx). Three reasons this stays out, permanently, not an oversight to
58	   * "fix" back in later:
59	   *   1. It uses the colour's display name as a raw CSS colour keyword — "Ivory" resolves as a
60	   *      real CSS colour, "Bay Blue" does not — which is both unauditable by `audit:tokens` and
61	   *      against this codebase's no-raw-design-value rule.
62	   *   2. In base it exists to tint the swatch behind a *missing* product image. This component is
63	   *      only ever rendered for colour variations that already have a populated image — the
64	   *      caller filters out any variation without one before rendering this component at all —
65	   *      so there is never a missing image for a fallback tint to show behind.
66	   *   3. Even if one slipped through, `background-size: cover` on the image (see the recipe's
67	   *      `image` part) would hide any tint sitting behind it regardless.
68	   */
69	  if (href) {
70	    return (
71	      <ColourSwatchLink
72	        to={href}
73	        __css={styles.swatch}
74	        role="radio"
75	        aria-checked={isSelected}
76	        aria-label={name}
77	        tabIndex={isFocusable ? 0 : -1}
78	        data-testid="colour-swatch"
79	      >
80	        {image}
81	      </ColourSwatchLink>
82	    );
83	  }
84	
85	  return (
86	    <chakra.span
87	      __css={styles.swatch}
88	      data-testid="colour-swatch"
89	    >
90	      {image}
91	    </chakra.span>
92	  );
93	};

content.text:
I don't have a safe way to get you a live-measured number — the real image URLs require SLAS-authenticated Shopper API calls, and I don't want to risk mishandling credentials from `.env.dev` just to fetch a test image. So this is a reasoned estimate from well-established figures, not a measurement — flagging that distinction clearly rather than presenting false precision.

**Per image:**
- A full-resolution fashion product photo served unscaled (what our build requests) is typically 150–500KB — SFCC master images are usually sourced at 1500–2000px+ for zoom/gallery use, at moderate-to-high JPEG quality.
- A 96px-wide DIS thumbnail at `q=60` (what `sizedSwatchUrl` requests) is typically 2–6KB — a small JPEG at that resolution and quality is reliably in that range.
- That's roughly a **30×–100× difference per image**, not a marginal one.

**Per page load:** both builds window pagination to a maximum of 4 rendered swatches at a time (`PAGE_SIZE = 4` in both), so a multi-colour PDP mounts up to 4 of these images on load, not the full colour count.

- Unsized (ours): ~4 × 300KB (mid-estimate) ≈ **~1.2MB** of avoidable image payload
- Sized (theirs): ~4 × 4KB ≈ **~16KB**

So the realistic gap is on the order of **several hundred KB to over a megabyte** of unnecessary data per PDP visit for any multi-colour product — on mobile, against a page that `AGENTS.md` explicitly calls out as having "mobile page speed" as "a top priority" and an LCP budget of ≤2s at p75.

**One caveat on LCP specifically:** the swatches themselves are very unlikely to *be* the LCP element (that's normally the main product image), so this may not show up as a direct LCP-metric regression. But it's still real, unnecessary page weight competing for mobile bandwidth and connection slots, and it's a plain violation of the written rule regardless of whether it happens to move the LCP number.

**To get an exact number cheaply:** open a real multi-colour PDP with DevTools Network open and check the swatch image request sizes directly — that'll give you the real figure for this catalogue's actual photography in under a minute, with your own already-authenticated session.

content.text:
Two different problems, two different fixes:

**The docs fix (already done)** — `plan.md` and `postbuild.md` for *this specific story* now say the right thing. That's like correcting a typo in one specific report after it's already printed.

**The DevImprover log (suggested, not yet done)** — is about *why the typo happened in the first place*, so it doesn't happen again on the next story.

Here's the actual mechanism: PostBuild's manifest audit ("does the diff match the plan?") runs once, at one specific point in the workflow — right after the build's originally-scoped commits finish. But real work kept happening *after* that point (the chevron gap was found, the token got added, the shared-constant fix landed) — all legitimate, all authorized, but none of it ever got checked against the manifest again. Nothing in `zimmerMANNPostBuild`'s own instructions says "re-run this check right before presenting to Marcel" — it only says to run it once, early.

That means the exact same gap will happen on the *next* story too. Any future build where something gets fixed after the main build phase closes — which is normal, it happens most of the time — will produce the same kind of stale audit, because the skill itself doesn't have a step that catches it.

Fixing `plan.md`/`postbuild.md` fixes SFCC-91's paperwork. Logging it in `zimmerMANNDevImprover` is how that observation turns into an actual edit to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`'s instructions — something like "re-run the manifest check as the last step, not just the first" — so the *skill* gets smarter, not just this one story's records.

Skipping the DevImprover step doesn't lose the current fix, but it does mean nobody remembers to check for this pattern next time — the log is what makes a second occurrence recognizable instead of a surprise.

- brief — PostBuild's manifest audit is never re-validated after later-authorized work lands — PROPOSED — pending

---

### PROCESS-1 — PostBuild's manifest audit runs once, early, and is never re-validated against later-authorized changes

`postbuild.md`'s "Whole-feature manifest audit" ran once, mid-build, and asserted "All 8 CREATE +
3 MODIFY files match exactly; all 14 excluded paths (`theme/foundation/`, ...) confirmed untouched
across every commit." That was true when it ran. It stopped being true two commits later
(`0fe3c2d`, `0aff491`), when a disabled-chevron gap was found post-audit and fixed with a
live-authorized Tier 1 token addition to `theme/foundation/colour.ts` + `zimmTokens.ts` — a
legitimate, properly-approved change, but one that landed in exactly the path the audit had just
certified as untouched. Nobody re-ran the manifest check afterward. The stale claim survived into
the PR being opened and was only caught when a `zimmerMANNReview` pass deliberately re-derived the
diff from source instead of trusting the prior audit.

**Attribution: BRIEF** — `zimmerMANNPostBuild/SKILL.md`'s Phase 2 manifest-versus-diff check (via
`zm-orchestrator`) has no instruction to re-run once Phase 6's review loop (or any other post-audit
fix round) adds commits outside the original manifest. The skill treats the manifest audit as a
one-time gate rather than a standing invariant that has to hold at hand-off time.

**Recurrence: first seen.** But the shape is generic, not specific to SFCC-91 — any build where a
real gap surfaces after the main build phase closes (which `handoff.md`'s own numbers say is
common: SFCC-91 alone had rework rounds on 2 of 4 steps, plus this post-hoc chevron fix) will
reproduce the same staleness unless the audit is re-run at hand-off, not just after the original
steps.

Evidence: `postbuild.md`'s manifest-audit paragraph (pre-correction) vs. the real diff
(`git diff 269d5d4..HEAD --numstat`, showing 9 CREATE / 5 non-registry MODIFY, not 8/3);
`plan.md` Decision #8 (added during this same review pass) documenting the live Tier 1
authorization that caused the drift; `zm-orchestrator`'s fresh scope-check output for PR #74,
which surfaced the discrepancy by refusing to trust the prior audit.

Disposition: **PROPOSED** — add a re-validation instruction to `zimmerMANNPostBuild/SKILL.md`.

**Proposed edit** — `zimmerMANNPostBuild/SKILL.md`, Phase 6 ("the review loop"), append after the
existing numbered steps:

```
**Before final hand-off, re-run the manifest check — not just once, at the end.** Phase 2's
manifest-versus-diff audit is a snapshot, not a standing guarantee. Any fix round in this phase
(a CodeRabbit rework, a reviewer's requested change, or a gap Marcel spots and Build fixes
directly) can add a file outside the original manifest — including a legitimate, individually-
authorized Tier 1/2 exception. If it does, that file belongs in the plan's manifest and in
postbuild.md's own audit paragraph, not left for the audit to silently go stale. Before presenting
the final state for merge, confirm the manifest audit's claim still matches `git diff
<base>..HEAD --numstat` exactly — if it doesn't, append a dated correction (same pattern as this
file's own "Open questions" section) rather than leaving the original claim uncorrected.
```

**Why:** would have caught SFCC-91's stale manifest claim before the PR was opened, instead of a
later `zimmerMANNReview` pass having to catch it by refusing to trust the prior audit.

  DevImprover pass. A full pass on SFCC-91 (or another ticket) may still turn up more.

Here's the whole thing from the top, plain language.

**What actually happened during the build:**

Partway through building SFCC-91, PostBuild ran a check: "does the code we built match exactly what the plan said we'd build — no more files, no fewer?" At that moment, the answer was yes, and it got written down: 8 new files, 3 changed files, nothing touched that shouldn't be.

*After* that check ran, you spotted a real gap (the pagination chevron had no disabled-colour treatment), and it got fixed properly — which meant adding a new design token to two Tier-1 files. You personally approved that as a verified Tier-1 approver. Completely legitimate, nothing broken.

But nobody went back and redid the "does everything match the plan" check after that fix landed. So the paperwork kept saying "8 files, 3 changes" even though the real, final answer was "9 files, 5 changes, two of them Tier-1." Nobody noticed until I ran a separate, unrelated check (for the PR #70-vs-#74 comparison) that deliberately didn't trust the old paperwork and looked at the real code instead — and the mismatch showed up.

**The 4 things I logged/edited — 3 are just paperwork corrections, 1 is different:**

| # | What it is | Does it touch any skill? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fixed `plan.md` to record the token decision that actually happened | No — just correcting SFCC-91's own file |
| 2 | Fixed `plan.md`'s file count to say 9/5 instead of the old 8/3 | No — same |
| 3 | Fixed `postbuild.md`'s claim so it doesn't say "confirmed untouched" about a file that was, legitimately, touched | No — same |
| 4 | Wrote down, in a separate "lessons learned" file, *why* 1–3 were needed | **This is the one with a proposed skill change** |

Items 1–3 are like correcting a receipt after you find a math error on it — they only fix SFCC-91's own records. Nothing about how future builds work changes because of them.

**Item 4 — the actual skill update being proposed:**

Right now, `zimmerMANNPostBuild`'s instructions say, in effect: *"check the file list against the plan once, partway through."* Nothing tells it to check again later.

The proposed fix adds exactly one thing: *"...and check it again, right before you're done, in case more work landed since the first check."*

Think of it like a kitchen that checks its inventory against its shopping list at the start of a shift, but never checks again at the end — even though more deliveries came in and more stuff got used throughout the day. The fix isn't a new rule about what's allowed in the kitchen. It's just: also look again before you lock up.

**What this update does NOT do:** it doesn't change what counts as a Tier 1 violation, doesn't add new restrictions, doesn't touch any other skill or agent, doesn't affect PR #74 or PR #70 in any way. It only adds a second checkpoint to `zimmerMANNPostBuild` so this exact kind of stale paperwork gets caught automatically on the next build, instead of only by accident.

That's the full scope of what you'd be approving — one added sentence-worth of instruction, in one skill, changing nothing else.

name: zimmerMANNPostBuild
description: The senior dev pass after a build. Audits what zimmerMANNBuild produced against zimmerMANNPreBuild's plan and findings, runs a whole-feature sweep for uniform defects, writes the PR body, and owns the review conversation — pushing and replying only on Marcel's go.
---

Marcel's own senior dev. Nothing built here — this skill judges what was built, writes what goes
public, and holds the conversation with CodeRabbit and the reviewer.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

**Input:** `$ARGUMENTS` — a Jira key. Reads three files under
`~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/`:

- **`handoff.md`** — Build's record: steps, commits, Scorer verdicts, rework rounds, gate numbers,
  UNIFORM findings, what went unverified
- **`plan.md`** — what was meant to be built
- **`findings.md`** — the gate table, with its 🟡 CLARIFY assumptions

If `handoff.md` is missing, Build either did not finish or ran before this was written. Say so and
reconstruct what you can from the branch's commits — but flag the audit as partial, because the
Scorer verdicts and UNIFORM findings are not recoverable from git.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get a five-agent sweep. Honour the scale the
plan chose. Nothing too crazy, no overthinking.

---

## Phase 1 — audit against both artefacts

Two documents, two different questions. Neither is covered by the loop that just ran.

### `findings.md` — did the gate hold?

Walk every row. For each:

- **🔴 BLOCKED** — was it resolved before Build started, and by what?
- **🟡 CLARIFY** — this is the one that matters. Each of these carried a **stated assumption** into
  the plan. **Did that assumption actually hold once the code existed?** Nothing else in the chain
  revisits them. An assumption that turned out wrong mid-build, that nobody went back to, is the
  most likely thing to reach the PR unnoticed.
- **🔵 NOTE** — still true? A note that has become a defect is a finding.

### `plan.md` — did the build deliver?

- Every step shipped what it promised, with its Scorer verdict.
- The diff matches the file manifest. Anything in the diff that isn't in the manifest is a scope
  finding — even if it looks correct.
- Every file's tier is what the plan said it was.
- **Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.** Never a finding.

Use `zm-orchestrator` for the manifest-versus-diff conformance pass. It already does exactly this
judgement at step scope.

---

## Phase 2 — the whole-feature sweep

Per-step scoring is **structurally blind** to a pattern applied consistently but wrongly: it
passes every individual review. On this project a systematic spacing error survived five commits
and every score, and was only found afterwards. This phase exists for that.

Run it in two directions, internal first.

### Internal — does the feature agree with itself?

No external rubric. One question: is this internally consistent?

- Every recipe the same shape — same `parts` convention, same registration, same naming
- Every component the same structure — export, props type, story, test
- Every token used the same way for the same purpose
- The same value not typed twice in two places

A divergence here is a finding even when both variants are individually defensible.

### External — does that shared shape conform?

Only once you know what the feature's own pattern *is*:

- **The exemplar PR** — does the feature match what it established? Where the exemplar is itself
  inconsistent, say which variant this work followed and whether that was the better choice. Do
  not report a divergence from an unstable pattern as a defect.
- **`.claude/rules/*`** — do the rules hold across the whole feature, not just per file?
- **Figma, end to end** — the rendered feature against the named nodes, every variant and state.
  Remember the node-type discriminator and never cross-compare the two Figma files.

Use `zm-tester` for this, fanning out across the feature rather than one step. Every finding
carries **UNIFORM** or **ONE-OFF** — at this scope, UNIFORM is what you are hunting.

---

## Phase 3 — if the audit fails

**Hand back to `zimmerMANNBuild`. Do not fix it here.**

The auditor becoming the author is exactly the independence that makes this phase worth running,
and Build has a Scorer and a rework cap that this skill does not.

Report the defect with its evidence, return the work, and **re-audit when it comes back.** A
re-audit is a fresh pass, not a check that the named item changed.

---

## Phase 4 — the PR

Write the body yourself. Do not call `/pr-checklist` — its output is the team's format, and this
one is yours.

**The body describes the diff that actually shipped, not the plan.** If the two differ, the diff
wins and the difference is worth a line.

Include: what changed and why · the tier of every touched file, with any Tier 2 approver named ·
what was tested and the real numbers · anything deliberately deferred, with the owning ticket ·
anything left unverified.

**Never in a PR title, body, commit message or code comment:**
- Claude attribution of any kind — no `Co-Authored-By`, no mention
- CodeRabbit mentions
- A citation of any local-only doc. `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md` and its predecessors are Marcel's
  personal files. Where the same rule exists in `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/rules/*`, cite that.
- Draft or pending disclaimers

Match the house standard by reading Marcel's own previously authored PRs on this repo, not by
inferring a format.

---

## Phase 5 — write it down, then present

**First write `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md`:**

```
# PostBuild — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Head: <sha>   Audited: <date>

## Audit — findings.md
| # | Gate item | Severity | Held? | Evidence |
<one row per row of findings.md. For every 🟡 CLARIFY: did the assumption hold?>

## Audit — plan.md
| Step | Delivered? | Commit | Notes |
<plus: files in the diff that were not in the manifest>

## Sweep — internal consistency
<does the feature agree with itself — recipes, structure, token use>

## Sweep — external conformance
<exemplar PR · .claude/rules/* · Figma end to end>

## UNIFORM findings
<the ones a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## PR body as written
<the exact text>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>
```

**Then append a block per review round**, as the loop runs:

```
## Round <n> — <date>
Findings received: <n> (CodeRabbit <n>, reviewer <n>)
| # | Finding | Verdict | Fixed in | Reply posted? |
<VALID / INVALID / OUT OF SCOPE / DEFER, with the evidence for each decline>
```

This file is read by **`zimmerMANNBuild rework`** — so it knows what was already declined and why,
rather than re-litigating it — and by **`zimmerMANNDevImprover`**. Write it even when the audit is
clean; a clean audit that left no record is indistinguishable from one that never ran.

## Then present

Give him, in **"ELI5 but I'm the FED Lead"** register:

1. The diff summary — files, tiers, commits
2. The audit result — every gate item and plan step, with anything that failed
3. The sweep result — **UNIFORM findings first**, they are the point of this skill
4. The proposed PR title and body
5. What could not be verified

Then **stop.**

**On his go: push and open the PR.** Not before. Push is the first irreversible, outward-facing
step in the chain, and it is his to authorise.

---

## Phase 6 — the review loop

When CodeRabbit or a reviewer requests changes:

1. **Hand the findings to `zimmerMANNBuild rework`.** It verifies each finding is real before
   anything is touched — CodeRabbit has run as low as 1-in-6 correct on this repo — then fixes and
   commits the valid ones.

2. **Draft a reply for every finding when it comes back.** Every thread gets a written answer:
   - **Fixed** — what changed, and the commit
   - **Declined** — the specific quotable repo rule, doc, or empirical result that makes it wrong.
     Not an opinion.
   - **Deferred** — the owning ticket or the person who decides

   **A fix commit with no in-thread reply does not count.** A prior PR here carried 18 threads with
   zero human replies; the process was being followed on the PR before it and was dropped entirely.

3. **Show him the full batch, then post on his go.** One approval covers the set.

4. Repeat until approved. If CodeRabbit raises the same objection a third time, stop re-running it
   and answer the threads instead — it has nothing to learn from unanswered comments.

---

## The owner rule — everywhere outward-facing

The audit report, the PR body, and every reply.

Every finding names **who resolves it**: Marcel, Tim, a designer, a BA, QA. A blocker owned by the
designer and one owned by Marcel need different actions.

**Where the owner is senior or lateral, phrase it as a question to them — never a directive.**
"Should this route via X, or have I misread it?" not "change this to X." Ask confirmatorily.

Before anything posts, count the asks. A review that mentions one person eight times reads as
hiding behind their authority.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never write code.** Every fix goes back to Build. This skill audits, writes, and posts.
- **Never push or post without an explicit go.** Both are outward-facing and irreversible in
  practice.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never re-litigate a settled decision.** If the plan decided it and the build honoured it, it
  is not a finding — report a *mechanical consequence* of a decision, never the decision.
- **Say what you could not verify.** An audit that finds nothing has not been shown to be capable
  of finding anything.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNReview

Review of a colleague's work. Same architecture as the build chain — ground truth, a gated audit,
then present and stop — tailored to a PR you did not write.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

**The thing that makes it work:** you hold the ground truth and the adjudication, and delegate only
the reading. Reviewers are cheap and fallible; measurements are expensive and authoritative. Keep
those on opposite sides of the line.

**Input:** `` — a PR number.

**Scale to the work.** A two-file PR does not get four reviewers. Nothing too crazy, no
overthinking.

---

## Phase 1 — ground truth. Yours, not an agent's.

### Frame the PR

Base SHA, head SHA, files changed, ±lines. **Use the live head** — a stale ref has already caused a
whole round of re-verification here.

### Requirements — Jira, Confluence, Figma

Build the same requirements picture a PreBuild would build, then judge the PR against it. Every
scope argument, every "this is missing", every "this wasn't asked for" gets decided against these
words — not the PR description's paraphrase of them.

**Jira.** Pull the full ticket: description, ACs, linked work items, and — critically — the full
comment thread. Decisions made in comments routinely contradict the description and never make it
back into the ACs. Flag: untestable ACs · requirements that contradict each other or the comments
· a linked blocker still open · a decision in comments that the implementation may not have seen.

**Confluence.** If the ticket links a PRD, TSD, or integration doc, read it. The Jira ACs are
often a summary; the full requirements live in Confluence. Flag: a Confluence requirement not
reflected in the ACs · a doc that contradicts the ticket · a doc that describes an approach the
PR does not follow.

**Figma.** Read the design systematically — not just the node cited in the PR description.

- **All variants and states:** hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, empty, selected.
  A state the PR doesn't implement is a finding; a state Figma doesn't specify is an open
  question to name, not a reason to skip.
- **Annotations:** interaction notes and spacing/token callouts often hold the real spec detail.
- **Currency:** is the linked node archived or superseded? An archived node that still renders
  is a trap — triage before judging.
- **Tokenisation:** does every colour, spacing, and type value map to an existing `--zimm-*`
  token, or did the author introduce a new one? A new token is Tier 1; confirm it was handled
  correctly.
- **Measurement:** FRAMES and INSTANCES report real boxes (comparable to CSS). TEXT nodes report
  cap-height (not comparable). Never file a mismatch from a TEXT node. Never cross-compare the
  Design System file and the Designs file — they are different sources.

**If the Jira-linked nodes are incomplete, partial, or outdated — stop and ask Marcel for the
correct nodes before continuing.** One node URL per variant and per state, not one per component.
Do not guess at a neighbouring node that looks close, do not proceed on a partial picture, and do
not treat an archived node as the spec. The whole review hangs on having the right design source;
a wrong node produces false findings and misses real ones. This is the one step where asking
beats estimating.

The visual checklist in Phase 2 tells you what to verify in the browser. This step tells you
**what to look for** — you cannot run that checklist without knowing what the design intended.

### The rubric

`.claude/rules/*`, `AGENTS.md`, and the exemplar PR the work should follow. These are what the PR
is judged against — a reviewer applying general best practice instead of house rules generates
noise that reads like signal.

**If the PR edits the rule files it would be judged against, read the rubric at the BASE commit.**
Judging a PR against its own edited rules is circular. Rule-file edits are reviewed separately, as
changes.

### Run the gates yourself — on head and on base

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test
npm run lint
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
```

Then run them again at the base SHA. **Without a baseline you cannot tell a failure the PR
introduced from one it inherited**, and inherited debt reported as a new violation is the fastest
way to lose a reviewer's trust.

Three false signals, all seen on this repo:

1. **Non-zero at a healthy baseline.** `lint` and `audit:tokens` both exit non-zero on a clean
   tree. Compare counts; ignore exit codes.
2. **A pass having run nothing.** `vitest.config.ts` sets `passWithNoTests: true` — a typo'd path
   filter exits 0 having run zero tests. **Assert on the reported item count, never the exit code.**
3. **A skipped required check looks green.** `detect-changes` can skip `unit-tests` and
   `storybook-test` entirely, and the PR still shows mergeable. Report which checks actually
   *executed* versus which were skipped. A skip proves nothing.

### CodeRabbit is an input, not a verdict

If CodeRabbit has reviewed, read it — then verify it. It has run as low as 1-in-6 correct on this
repo. Its findings enter Phase 2 as claims to test, exactly like anyone else's.

---

## Phase 2 — audit

### Fan out

`zm-tester` dispatches reviewers on **distinct but overlapping** briefs. The overlap is the
mechanism: two agents converging independently is your confidence signal; two disagreeing is where
you learn something.

Give each: the diff, the ticket verbatim, and **your measured gate numbers — then forbid them from
re-running the gates.** Their budget goes on what the gates cannot see.

Angles that have earned their place: correctness and regression · conventions, structure and tier
ownership · contract fidelity, if the PR ports, wraps or overrides something · failure modes and
security · token and styling strategy (bandaid tokens, missing semantic tokens, state
exhaustiveness).

**Design fidelity is yours, not an agent's.** Agents have no browser and no Figma access — ask
them to reason from code and they will, but they cannot see what renders. For any PR that changes
rendered output, run this checklist yourself at the PR's head:

| What to check | How |
|---|---|
| Dimensions and spacing match Figma frames | DevTools computed, vs. Figma inspect |
| Colours resolve to the correct semantic token | DevTools → Computed → colour value |
| Typography uses `textStyle=`, not raw `fontSize` | DevTools → font-size is a `var()` |
| All designed states render correctly (hover, focus, active, disabled) | Tab through + `:hov` in DevTools |
| Responsive behaviour matches the spec | Resize or toggle responsive mode |
| No visual regressions on adjacent components | Scroll the surrounding page |

If a state is not in the PR's recipe at all, no agent will flag it — only you will notice. The
visual checkpoint is the only gate on design fidelity.

Use **fresh contexts, not forks.** A fork inherits your assumptions about what "done" looks like,
which is exactly what you want tested.

### Scope

`zm-orchestrator` returns the scope verdict — does this PR deliver its ticket, neither under nor
over. Both directions carry equal weight.

### Verify the findings before they reach you

`zm-scorer`, briefed in **findings mode** — it is not scoring the PR, it is scoring the claims:

> For each finding: does it survive scrutiny? Reproduce it or say you could not. Return
> **CONFIRMED** (reproduced from source), **PLAUSIBLE** (consistent with what you read, decisive
> evidence missing — say exactly what would settle it), or **UNSUPPORTED** (the citation does not
> support the claim; say what is actually true). Where a finding's conclusion is broader than its
> search supports, downgrade it — that is the single most common failure mode. Any "X exists
> nowhere" claim must state its search scope in the same sentence.

Expect roughly a third to be wrong. You should not be adjudicating unverified claims.

### Classify every survivor

- **In-scope defect** — belongs to this PR. Only these can become comments.
- **Out-of-scope** — real, but not this PR's problem. Name the owning ticket or the person.
- **Nitpick** — cosmetic, brings no value. Recorded, never posted.

A true finding raised on the wrong PR is still noise.

---

## Phase 3 — adjudicate

### Present, in "ELI5 but I'm the FED Lead" register

1. **Gate table** — head versus base, with which checks actually executed
2. **Findings, ranked by what it costs to ignore** — not by severity label, by consequence.
   Each with `file:line`, CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE, and its classification
3. **The scope verdict**
4. **What nobody verified** — the honest section, and what stops a clean result reading as proof
5. **Your adjudications to make**, one at a time via AskUserQuestion

### The verdict is yours

**Approve or request changes is your call, and so is every disputed finding.** The agents produce
findings; you decide what they mean. Where two reviewers disagree, go to source yourself — do not
average them, and do not take the more confident one. Confidence and correctness are not correlated
in agent output.

Name one premise every reviewer agreed on, and make someone attack it.

### Then the comments

Draft general and inline comments for the in-scope defects only. Structure that has worked:

- Verdict up front
- The small cleanups separated from the one thing that genuinely needs the author's call
- A blocker framed as **a question about intent**, citing the project's own doc by section
- The two acceptable resolutions named
- Where an independent tool corroborated, say so

**Natural human language without sacrificing the technical accuracy.** No em-dashes. No Claude or
CodeRabbit attribution. No citation of any local-only doc — cite `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/rules/*`
instead, which the author can actually open.

**Nothing posts until you say so.** Show the full set, post the batch on your go.

---

## The loop

The author pushes changes. Re-review.

**Scoped by default:** which findings the new commits resolved, which they missed, and whether the
fixes introduced anything new. Settled items are not re-litigated.

**Full pass when the diff has genuinely moved** — a substantial new commit, or a change to the
approach rather than the details. **Say which one you ran.**

Repeat until approved. Confirm your own requested changes actually landed rather than taking
"done" on trust.

---

## Ownership and phrasing — every outward-facing surface

Every finding names **who resolves it**: the author, Tim, a designer, a BA, QA.

**Where the owner is senior or lateral, phrase it as a question — never a directive.** "Should this
route via X, or have I misread it?" not "change this to X." Ask confirmatorily.

Before posting, count the asks. A review that mentions one person eight times reads as hiding
behind their authority.

**Be scrupulously fair to the author.** Separate "broke a documented rule" from "hit a gap the
process never covered", and where the process failed them, say so. Flag explicitly any finding
where the fact is true but the characterisation is unfair — better to drop a finding than post an
unfair one.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never write code.** This skill reviews. If a fix is needed on your own branch, that is Build.
- **Never post a comment, a review, or a verdict without an explicit go.**
- **Never resolve a thread you did not open.**
- **Never report inherited debt as a new violation.** Baseline first.
- **Never flag out-of-scope findings onto the PR.** Record them for yourself.
- **Say what you could not verify.** A review that finds nothing has not been shown to be capable
  of finding anything.
